# synstructure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/synstructure/0.13.2/target-redirect/synstructure/

## Expand description

This crate provides helper types for matching against enum variants, and extracting bindings to each of the fields in the deriving Struct or Enum in a generic way.

If you are writing a `#[derive]` which needs to perform some operation on
every field, then you have come to the right place!

[§](https://docs.rs#example-walkfields)Example: `WalkFields`

[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementation)Trait Implementation

```
pub trait WalkFields: std::any::Any {
    fn walk_fields(&self, walk: &mut FnMut(&WalkFields));
}
impl WalkFields for i32 {
    fn walk_fields(&self, _walk: &mut FnMut(&WalkFields)) {}
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-derive)Custom Derive

```
fn walkfields_derive(s: synstructure::Structure) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    let body = s.each(|bi| quote!{
        walk(#bi)
    });
    s.gen_impl(quote! {
        extern crate synstructure_test_traits;
        gen impl synstructure_test_traits::WalkFields for @Self {
            fn walk_fields(&self, walk: &mut FnMut(&synstructure_test_traits::WalkFields)) {
                match *self { #body }
            }
        }
    })
}
synstructure::decl_derive!([WalkFields] => walkfields_derive);
/*
 * Test Case
 */
fn main() {
    synstructure::test_derive! {
        walkfields_derive {
            enum A<T> {
                B(i32, T),
                C(i32),
            }
        }
        expands to {
            const _: () = {
                extern crate synstructure_test_traits;
                impl<T> synstructure_test_traits::WalkFields for A<T>
                    where T: synstructure_test_traits::WalkFields
                {
                    fn walk_fields(&self, walk: &mut FnMut(&synstructure_test_traits::WalkFields)) {
                        match *self {
                            A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,) => {
                                { walk(__binding_0) }
                                { walk(__binding_1) }
                            }
                            A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
                                { walk(__binding_0) }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            };
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-interest)Example: `Interest`

[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementation-1)Trait Implementation

```
pub trait Interest {
    fn interesting(&self) -> bool;
}
impl Interest for i32 {
    fn interesting(&self) -> bool { *self > 0 }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-derive-1)Custom Derive

```
fn interest_derive(mut s: synstructure::Structure) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    let body = s.fold(false, |acc, bi| quote!{
        #acc || synstructure_test_traits::Interest::interesting(#bi)
    });
    s.gen_impl(quote! {
        extern crate synstructure_test_traits;
        gen impl synstructure_test_traits::Interest for @Self {
            fn interesting(&self) -> bool {
                match *self {
                    #body
                }
            }
        }
    })
}
synstructure::decl_derive!([Interest] => interest_derive);
/*
 * Test Case
 */
fn main() {
    synstructure::test_derive!{
        interest_derive {
            enum A<T> {
                B(i32, T),
                C(i32),
            }
        }
        expands to {
            const _: () = {
                extern crate synstructure_test_traits;
                impl<T> synstructure_test_traits::Interest for A<T>
                    where T: synstructure_test_traits::Interest
                {
                    fn interesting(&self) -> bool {
                        match *self {
                            A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,) => {
                                false ||
                                    synstructure_test_traits::Interest::interesting(__binding_0) ||
                                    synstructure_test_traits::Interest::interesting(__binding_1)
                            }
                            A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
                                false ||
                                    synstructure_test_traits::Interest::interesting(__binding_0)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            };
        }
    }
}
```
For more example usage, consider investigating the `abomonation_derive` crate,
which makes use of this crate, and is fairly simple.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_attribute.html)- attribute
- The `decl_attribute!`macro declares a custom attribute wrapper. It will parse the incoming`TokenStream`into a`synstructure::Structure`object, and pass it into the inner function.
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_derive.html)- derive
- The `decl_derive!`macro declares a custom derive wrapper. It will parse the incoming`TokenStream`into a`synstructure::Structure`object, and pass it into the inner function.
- [test_](https://docs.rs/macro.test_derive.html)- derive
- Run a test on a custom derive. This macro expands both the original struct and the expansion to ensure that they compile correctly, and confirms that feeding the original struct into the named derive will produce the written output.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Binding](https://docs.rs/struct.BindingInfo.html)- Info
- Information about a specific binding. This contains both an `Ident`reference to the given field, and the syn`&'a Field`descriptor for that field.
- [Structure](https://docs.rs/struct.Structure.html)
- A wrapper around a `syn::DeriveInput`which provides utilities for creating custom derive trait implementations.
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/struct.VariantAst.html)- Ast
- This type is similar to `syn`’s`Variant`type, however each of the fields are references rather than owned. When this is used as the AST for a real variant, this struct simply borrows the fields of the`syn::Variant`, however this type may also be used as the sole variant for a struct.
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/struct.VariantInfo.html)- Info
- A wrapper around a `syn::DeriveInput`’s variant which provides utilities for destructuring`Variant`s with`match`expressions.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Macro](https://docs.rs/trait.MacroResult.html)- Result
- Helper trait describing values which may be returned by macro implementation methods used by this crate’s macros.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [unpretty_](https://docs.rs/fn.unpretty_print.html)- print
- Dumps an unpretty version of a tokenstream. Takes any type which implements
`Display`.

[132](https://docs.rs#132)//!                                     synstructure_test_traits::Interest::interesting(__binding_1)
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!                             }
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!                             A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//!                                 false ||
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!                                     synstructure_test_traits::Interest::interesting(__binding_0)
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//!                             }
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//!                         }
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//!                     }
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//!                 }
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!             };
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!         }
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//!     }
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//! }
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//! ```
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//!
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//! For more example usage, consider investigating the `abomonation_derive` crate,
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//! which makes use of this crate, and is fairly simple.
[149](https://docs.rs#149)

[151](https://docs.rs#151)    clippy::default_trait_access,

[154](https://docs.rs#154)    clippy::must_use_candidate,
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    clippy::needless_pass_by_value
[156](https://docs.rs#156))]

[205](https://docs.rs#205)/// The type of binding to use when generating a pattern.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[207](https://docs.rs#207)pub enum BindStyle {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    /// `x`
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    Move,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// `mut x`
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    MoveMut,
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    /// `ref x`
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    Ref,
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    /// `ref mut x`
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    RefMut,
[216](https://docs.rs#216)}
[217](https://docs.rs#217)
[218](https://docs.rs#218)impl ToTokens for BindStyle {
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    fn to_tokens(&self, tokens: &mut TokenStream) {
[220](https://docs.rs#220)        match self {
[221](https://docs.rs#221)            BindStyle::Move => {}
[222](https://docs.rs#222)            BindStyle::MoveMut => quote_spanned!(Span::call_site() => mut).to_tokens(tokens),
[223](https://docs.rs#223)            BindStyle::Ref => quote_spanned!(Span::call_site() => ref).to_tokens(tokens),
[224](https://docs.rs#224)            BindStyle::RefMut => quote_spanned!(Span::call_site() => ref mut).to_tokens(tokens),
[225](https://docs.rs#225)        }
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    }
[227](https://docs.rs#227)}
[228](https://docs.rs#228)
[229](https://docs.rs#229)// Internal method for merging seen_generics arrays together.
[230](https://docs.rs#230)fn generics_fuse(res: &mut Vec<bool>, new: &[bool]) {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    for (i, &flag) in new.iter().enumerate() {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        if i == res.len() {
[233](https://docs.rs#233)            res.push(false);
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        }
[235](https://docs.rs#235)        if flag {
[236](https://docs.rs#236)            res[i] = true;
[237](https://docs.rs#237)        }
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    }
[239](https://docs.rs#239)}
[240](https://docs.rs#240)
[241](https://docs.rs#241)// Internal method for extracting the set of generics which have been matched.
[242](https://docs.rs#242)fn fetch_generics<'a>(set: &[bool], generics: &'a Generics) -> Vec<&'a Ident> {
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    let mut tys = vec![];
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    for (&seen, param) in set.iter().zip(generics.params.iter()) {
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        if seen {
[246](https://docs.rs#246)            if let GenericParam::Type(tparam) = param {
[247](https://docs.rs#247)                tys.push(&tparam.ident);
[248](https://docs.rs#248)            }
[249](https://docs.rs#249)        }
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    }
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    tys
[252](https://docs.rs#252)}
[253](https://docs.rs#253)
[254](https://docs.rs#254)// Internal method to merge two Generics objects together intelligently.
[255](https://docs.rs#255)fn merge_generics(into: &mut Generics, from: &Generics) -> Result<()> {
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    // Try to add the param into `into`, and merge parmas with identical names.
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    for p in &from.params {
[258](https://docs.rs#258)        for op in &into.params {
[259](https://docs.rs#259)            match (op, p) {
[260](https://docs.rs#260)                (GenericParam::Type(otp), GenericParam::Type(tp)) => {
[261](https://docs.rs#261)                    // NOTE: This is only OK because syn ignores the span for equality purposes.
[262](https://docs.rs#262)                    if otp.ident == tp.ident {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)                        return Err(Error::new_spanned(
[264](https://docs.rs#264)                            p,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)                            format!(
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                                "Attempted to merge conflicting generic parameters: {} and {}",
[267](https://docs.rs#267)                                quote!(#op),
[268](https://docs.rs#268)                                quote!(#p)
[269](https://docs.rs#269)                            ),
[270](https://docs.rs#270)                        ));
[271](https://docs.rs#271)                    }
[272](https://docs.rs#272)                }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)                (GenericParam::Lifetime(olp), GenericParam::Lifetime(lp)) => {
[274](https://docs.rs#274)                    // NOTE: This is only OK because syn ignores the span for equality purposes.
[275](https://docs.rs#275)                    if olp.lifetime == lp.lifetime {
[276](https://docs.rs#276)                        return Err(Error::new_spanned(
[277](https://docs.rs#277)                            p,
[278](https://docs.rs#278)                            format!(
[279](https://docs.rs#279)                                "Attempted to merge conflicting generic parameters: {} and {}",
[280](https://docs.rs#280)                                quote!(#op),
[281](https://docs.rs#281)                                quote!(#p)
[282](https://docs.rs#282)                            ),
[283](https://docs.rs#283)                        ));
[284](https://docs.rs#284)                    }
[285](https://docs.rs#285)                }
[286](https://docs.rs#286)                // We don't support merging Const parameters, because that wouldn't make much sense.
[287](https://docs.rs#287)                _ => (),
[288](https://docs.rs#288)            }
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        }
[290](https://docs.rs#290)        into.params.push(p.clone());
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    }
[292](https://docs.rs#292)
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    // Add any where clauses from the input generics object.
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    if let Some(from_clause) = &from.where_clause {
[295](https://docs.rs#295)        into.make_where_clause()
[296](https://docs.rs#296)            .predicates
[297](https://docs.rs#297)            .extend(from_clause.predicates.iter().cloned());
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    }
[299](https://docs.rs#299)
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    Ok(())
[301](https://docs.rs#301)}
[302](https://docs.rs#302)
[303](https://docs.rs#303)/// Helper method which does the same thing as rustc 1.20's
[304](https://docs.rs#304)/// `Option::get_or_insert_with`. This method is used to keep backwards
[305](https://docs.rs#305)/// compatibility with rustc 1.15.
[306](https://docs.rs#306)fn get_or_insert_with<T, F>(opt: &mut Option<T>, f: F) -> &mut T
[307](https://docs.rs#307)where
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    F: FnOnce() -> T,
[309](https://docs.rs#309){
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    if opt.is_none() {
[311](https://docs.rs#311)        *opt = Some(f());
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    }
[313](https://docs.rs#313)
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    match opt {
[315](https://docs.rs#315)        Some(v) => v,
[316](https://docs.rs#316)        None => unreachable!(),
[317](https://docs.rs#317)    }
[318](https://docs.rs#318)}
[319](https://docs.rs#319)
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// Information about a specific binding. This contains both an `Ident`
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// reference to the given field, and the syn `&'a Field` descriptor for that
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// field.
[323](https://docs.rs#323)///
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// This type supports `quote::ToTokens`, so can be directly used within the
[325](https://docs.rs#325)/// `quote!` macro. It expands to a reference to the matched field.
[326](https://docs.rs#326)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[327](https://docs.rs#327)pub struct BindingInfo<'a> {
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    /// The name which this `BindingInfo` will bind to.
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    pub binding: Ident,
[330](https://docs.rs#330)
[331](https://docs.rs#331)    /// The type of binding which this `BindingInfo` will create.
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    pub style: BindStyle,
[333](https://docs.rs#333)
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    field: &'a Field,
[335](https://docs.rs#335)
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    // These are used to determine which type parameters are avaliable.
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    generics: &'a Generics,
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    seen_generics: Vec<bool>,
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    // The original index of the binding
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    // this will not change when .filter() is called
[341](https://docs.rs#341)    index: usize,
[342](https://docs.rs#342)}
[343](https://docs.rs#343)
[344](https://docs.rs#344)impl ToTokens for BindingInfo<'_> {
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    fn to_tokens(&self, tokens: &mut TokenStream) {
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        self.binding.to_tokens(tokens);
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    }
[348](https://docs.rs#348)}
[349](https://docs.rs#349)
[350](https://docs.rs#350)impl<'a> BindingInfo<'a> {
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    /// Returns a reference to the underlying `syn` AST node which this
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    /// `BindingInfo` references
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    pub fn ast(&self) -> &'a Field {
[354](https://docs.rs#354)        self.field
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    }
[356](https://docs.rs#356)
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    /// Generates the pattern fragment for this field binding.
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    ///
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    /// # Example
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    /// ```
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    ///     enum A {
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    ///         B{ a: i32, b: i32 },
[365](https://docs.rs#365)    ///         C(u32),
[366](https://docs.rs#366)    ///     }
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    /// };
[368](https://docs.rs#368)    /// let s = Structure::new(&di);
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    ///
[370](https://docs.rs#370)    /// assert_eq!(
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    ///     s.variants()[0].bindings()[0].pat().to_string(),
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    ///     quote! {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)    ///         ref __binding_0
[374](https://docs.rs#374)    ///     }.to_string()
[375](https://docs.rs#375)    /// );
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    /// ```
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    pub fn pat(&self) -> TokenStream {
[378](https://docs.rs#378)        let BindingInfo { binding, style, .. } = self;
[379](https://docs.rs#379)        quote!(#style #binding)
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    }
[381](https://docs.rs#381)
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    /// Returns a list of the type parameters which are referenced in this
[383](https://docs.rs#383)    /// field's type.
[384](https://docs.rs#384)    ///
[385](https://docs.rs#385)    /// # Caveat
[386](https://docs.rs#386)    ///
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    /// If the field contains any macros in type position, all parameters will
[388](https://docs.rs#388)    /// be considered bound. This is because we cannot determine which type
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    /// parameters are bound by type macros.
[390](https://docs.rs#390)    ///
[391](https://docs.rs#391)    /// # Example
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    /// ```
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    ///     struct A<T, U> {
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    ///         a: Option<T>,
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    ///         b: U,
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    ///     }
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// };
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    ///
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    /// assert_eq!(
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    ///     s.variants()[0].bindings()[0].referenced_ty_params(),
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    ///     &["e::format_ident!("T")]
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    /// );
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// ```
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    pub fn referenced_ty_params(&self) -> Vec<&'a Ident> {
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        fetch_generics(&self.seen_generics, self.generics)
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    }
[410](https://docs.rs#410)}
[411](https://docs.rs#411)
[412](https://docs.rs#412)/// This type is similar to `syn`'s `Variant` type, however each of the fields
[413](https://docs.rs#413)/// are references rather than owned. When this is used as the AST for a real
[414](https://docs.rs#414)/// variant, this struct simply borrows the fields of the `syn::Variant`,
[415](https://docs.rs#415)/// however this type may also be used as the sole variant for a struct.
[416](https://docs.rs#416)#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[417](https://docs.rs#417)pub struct VariantAst<'a> {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    pub attrs: &'a [Attribute],
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    pub ident: &'a Ident,
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    pub fields: &'a Fields,
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    pub discriminant: &'a Option<(token::Eq, Expr)>,
[422](https://docs.rs#422)}
[423](https://docs.rs#423)
[424](https://docs.rs#424)/// A wrapper around a `syn::DeriveInput`'s variant which provides utilities
[425](https://docs.rs#425)/// for destructuring `Variant`s with `match` expressions.
[426](https://docs.rs#426)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[427](https://docs.rs#427)pub struct VariantInfo<'a> {
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    pub prefix: Option<&'a Ident>,
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    bindings: Vec<BindingInfo<'a>>,
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    ast: VariantAst<'a>,
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    generics: &'a Generics,
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    // The original length of `bindings` before any `.filter()` calls
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    original_length: usize,
[434](https://docs.rs#434)}
[435](https://docs.rs#435)
[436](https://docs.rs#436)/// Helper function used by the `VariantInfo` constructor. Walks all of the types
[437](https://docs.rs#437)/// in `field` and returns a list of the type parameters from `ty_params` which
[438](https://docs.rs#438)/// are referenced in the field.
[439](https://docs.rs#439)fn get_ty_params(field: &Field, generics: &Generics) -> Vec<bool> {
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    // Helper type. Discovers all identifiers inside of the visited type,
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    // and calls a callback with them.
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    struct BoundTypeLocator<'a> {
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        result: Vec<bool>,
[444](https://docs.rs#444)        generics: &'a Generics,
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    }
[446](https://docs.rs#446)
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    impl<'a> Visit<'a> for BoundTypeLocator<'a> {
[448](https://docs.rs#448)        // XXX: This also (intentionally) captures paths like T::SomeType. Is
[449](https://docs.rs#449)        // this desirable?
[450](https://docs.rs#450)        fn visit_ident(&mut self, id: &Ident) {
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            for (idx, i) in self.generics.params.iter().enumerate() {
[452](https://docs.rs#452)                if let GenericParam::Type(tparam) = i {
[453](https://docs.rs#453)                    if tparam.ident == *id {
[454](https://docs.rs#454)                        self.result[idx] = true;
[455](https://docs.rs#455)                    }
[456](https://docs.rs#456)                }
[457](https://docs.rs#457)            }
[458](https://docs.rs#458)        }
[459](https://docs.rs#459)
[460](https://docs.rs#460)        fn visit_type_macro(&mut self, x: &'a TypeMacro) {
[461](https://docs.rs#461)            // If we see a type_mac declaration, then we can't know what type parameters
[462](https://docs.rs#462)            // it might be binding, so we presume it binds all of them.
[463](https://docs.rs#463)            for r in &mut self.result {
[464](https://docs.rs#464)                *r = true;
[465](https://docs.rs#465)            }
[466](https://docs.rs#466)            visit::visit_type_macro(self, x);
[467](https://docs.rs#467)        }
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    }
[469](https://docs.rs#469)
[470](https://docs.rs#470)    let mut btl = BoundTypeLocator {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)        result: vec![false; generics.params.len()],
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        generics,
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    };
[474](https://docs.rs#474)
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    btl.visit_type(&field.ty);
[476](https://docs.rs#476)
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    btl.result
[478](https://docs.rs#478)}
[479](https://docs.rs#479)
[480](https://docs.rs#480)impl<'a> VariantInfo<'a> {
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    fn new(ast: VariantAst<'a>, prefix: Option<&'a Ident>, generics: &'a Generics) -> Self {
[482](https://docs.rs#482)        let bindings = match ast.fields {
[483](https://docs.rs#483)            Fields::Unit => vec![],
[484](https://docs.rs#484)            Fields::Unnamed(FieldsUnnamed {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)                unnamed: fields, ..
[486](https://docs.rs#486)            })
[487](https://docs.rs#487)            | Fields::Named(FieldsNamed { named: fields, .. }) => {
[488](https://docs.rs#488)                fields
[489](https://docs.rs#489)                    .into_iter()
[490](https://docs.rs#490)                    .enumerate()
[491](https://docs.rs#491)                    .map(|(i, field)| {
[492](https://docs.rs#492)                        // XXX: binding_span has to be call_site to avoid privacy
[493](https://docs.rs#493)                        // when deriving on private fields, but be located at the field
[494](https://docs.rs#494)                        // span for nicer diagnostics.
[495](https://docs.rs#495)                        let binding_span = Span::call_site().located_at(field.span());
[496](https://docs.rs#496)                        BindingInfo {
[497](https://docs.rs#497)                            binding: format_ident!("__binding_{}", i, span = binding_span),
[498](https://docs.rs#498)                            style: BindStyle::Ref,
[499](https://docs.rs#499)                            field,
[500](https://docs.rs#500)                            generics,
[501](https://docs.rs#501)                            seen_generics: get_ty_params(field, generics),
[502](https://docs.rs#502)                            index: i,
[503](https://docs.rs#503)                        }
[504](https://docs.rs#504)                    })
[505](https://docs.rs#505)                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
[506](https://docs.rs#506)            }
[507](https://docs.rs#507)        };
[508](https://docs.rs#508)
[509](https://docs.rs#509)        let original_length = bindings.len();
[510](https://docs.rs#510)        VariantInfo {
[511](https://docs.rs#511)            prefix,
[512](https://docs.rs#512)            bindings,
[513](https://docs.rs#513)            ast,
[514](https://docs.rs#514)            generics,
[515](https://docs.rs#515)            original_length,
[516](https://docs.rs#516)        }
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    }
[518](https://docs.rs#518)
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    /// Returns a slice of the bindings in this Variant.
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    pub fn bindings(&self) -> &[BindingInfo<'a>] {
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        &self.bindings
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    }
[523](https://docs.rs#523)
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    /// Returns a mut slice of the bindings in this Variant.
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    pub fn bindings_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [BindingInfo<'a>] {
[526](https://docs.rs#526)        &mut self.bindings
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    }
[528](https://docs.rs#528)
[529](https://docs.rs#529)    /// Returns a `VariantAst` object which contains references to the
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// underlying `syn` AST node which this `Variant` was created from.
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    pub fn ast(&self) -> VariantAst<'a> {
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        self.ast
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    }
[534](https://docs.rs#534)
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    /// True if any bindings were omitted due to a `filter` call.
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    pub fn omitted_bindings(&self) -> bool {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        self.original_length != self.bindings.len()
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    }
[539](https://docs.rs#539)
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    /// Generates the match-arm pattern which could be used to match against this Variant.
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    ///
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    /// # Example
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    /// ```
[544](https://docs.rs#544)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    ///     enum A {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[548](https://docs.rs#548)    ///         C(u32),
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    ///     }
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    /// };
[551](https://docs.rs#551)    /// let s = Structure::new(&di);
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    ///
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    /// assert_eq!(
[554](https://docs.rs#554)    ///     s.variants()[0].pat().to_string(),
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    ///     quote!{
[556](https://docs.rs#556)    ///         A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,)
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    ///     }.to_string()
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    /// );
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    /// ```
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    pub fn pat(&self) -> TokenStream {
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        let mut t = TokenStream::new();
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        if let Some(prefix) = self.prefix {
[563](https://docs.rs#563)            prefix.to_tokens(&mut t);
[564](https://docs.rs#564)            quote!(::).to_tokens(&mut t);
[565](https://docs.rs#565)        }
[566](https://docs.rs#566)        self.ast.ident.to_tokens(&mut t);
[567](https://docs.rs#567)        match self.ast.fields {
[568](https://docs.rs#568)            Fields::Unit => {
[569](https://docs.rs#569)                assert!(self.bindings.is_empty());
[570](https://docs.rs#570)            }
[571](https://docs.rs#571)            Fields::Unnamed(..) => token::Paren(Span::call_site()).surround(&mut t, |t| {
[572](https://docs.rs#572)                let mut expected_index = 0;
[573](https://docs.rs#573)                for binding in &self.bindings {
[574](https://docs.rs#574)                    while expected_index < binding.index {
[575](https://docs.rs#575)                        quote!(_,).to_tokens(t);
[576](https://docs.rs#576)                        expected_index += 1;
[577](https://docs.rs#577)                    }
[578](https://docs.rs#578)                    binding.pat().to_tokens(t);
[579](https://docs.rs#579)                    quote!(,).to_tokens(t);
[580](https://docs.rs#580)                    expected_index += 1;
[581](https://docs.rs#581)                }
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                if expected_index != self.original_length {
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                    quote!(..).to_tokens(t);
[584](https://docs.rs#584)                }
[585](https://docs.rs#585)            }),
[586](https://docs.rs#586)            Fields::Named(..) => token::Brace(Span::call_site()).surround(&mut t, |t| {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                for binding in &self.bindings {
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                    binding.field.ident.to_tokens(t);
[589](https://docs.rs#589)                    quote!(:).to_tokens(t);
[590](https://docs.rs#590)                    binding.pat().to_tokens(t);
[591](https://docs.rs#591)                    quote!(,).to_tokens(t);
[592](https://docs.rs#592)                }
[593](https://docs.rs#593)                if self.omitted_bindings() {
[594](https://docs.rs#594)                    quote!(..).to_tokens(t);
[595](https://docs.rs#595)                }
[596](https://docs.rs#596)            }),
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        }
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        t
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    }
[600](https://docs.rs#600)
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    /// Generates the token stream required to construct the current variant.
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    ///
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    /// The init array initializes each of the fields in the order they are
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    /// written in `variant.ast().fields`.
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    ///
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    /// # Example
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    /// ```
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    ///     enum A {
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    ///         B(usize, usize),
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    ///         C{ v: usize },
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    ///     }
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    /// };
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    /// let s = Structure::new(&di);
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    ///
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    /// assert_eq!(
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    ///     s.variants()[0].construct(|_, i| quote!(#i)).to_string(),
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    ///
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    ///     quote!{
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    ///         A::B(0usize, 1usize,)
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    ///     }.to_string()
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    /// );
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    ///
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// assert_eq!(
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    ///     s.variants()[1].construct(|_, i| quote!(#i)).to_string(),
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    ///
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    ///     quote!{
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    ///         A::C{ v: 0usize, }
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    ///     }.to_string()
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    /// );
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    /// ```
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    pub fn construct<F, T>(&self, mut func: F) -> TokenStream
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    where
[635](https://docs.rs#635)        F: FnMut(&Field, usize) -> T,
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        T: ToTokens,
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    {
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        let mut t = TokenStream::new();
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        if let Some(prefix) = self.prefix {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            quote!(#prefix ::).to_tokens(&mut t);
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        }
[642](https://docs.rs#642)        self.ast.ident.to_tokens(&mut t);
[643](https://docs.rs#643)
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        match &self.ast.fields {
[645](https://docs.rs#645)            Fields::Unit => (),
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            Fields::Unnamed(FieldsUnnamed { unnamed, .. }) => {
[647](https://docs.rs#647)                token::Paren::default().surround(&mut t, |t| {
[648](https://docs.rs#648)                    for (i, field) in unnamed.into_iter().enumerate() {
[649](https://docs.rs#649)                        func(field, i).to_tokens(t);
[650](https://docs.rs#650)                        quote!(,).to_tokens(t);
[651](https://docs.rs#651)                    }
[652](https://docs.rs#652)                });
[653](https://docs.rs#653)            }
[654](https://docs.rs#654)            Fields::Named(FieldsNamed { named, .. }) => {
[655](https://docs.rs#655)                token::Brace::default().surround(&mut t, |t| {
[656](https://docs.rs#656)                    for (i, field) in named.into_iter().enumerate() {
[657](https://docs.rs#657)                        field.ident.to_tokens(t);
[658](https://docs.rs#658)                        quote!(:).to_tokens(t);
[659](https://docs.rs#659)                        func(field, i).to_tokens(t);
[660](https://docs.rs#660)                        quote!(,).to_tokens(t);
[661](https://docs.rs#661)                    }
[662](https://docs.rs#662)                });
[663](https://docs.rs#663)            }
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        }
[665](https://docs.rs#665)        t
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    }
[667](https://docs.rs#667)
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    /// Runs the passed-in function once for each bound field, passing in a `BindingInfo`.
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    /// and generating a `match` arm which evaluates the returned tokens.
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    ///
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    /// This method will ignore fields which are ignored through the `filter`
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    /// method.
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    ///
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    /// # Example
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    /// ```
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    ///     enum A {
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    ///         C(u32),
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    ///     }
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    /// };
[683](https://docs.rs#683)    /// let s = Structure::new(&di);
[684](https://docs.rs#684)    ///
[685](https://docs.rs#685)    /// assert_eq!(
[686](https://docs.rs#686)    ///     s.variants()[0].each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    ///
[688](https://docs.rs#688)    ///     quote!{
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    ///         A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,) => {
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[691](https://docs.rs#691)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_1) }
[692](https://docs.rs#692)    ///         }
[693](https://docs.rs#693)    ///     }.to_string()
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    /// );
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    /// ```
[696](https://docs.rs#696)    pub fn each<F, R>(&self, mut f: F) -> TokenStream
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    where
[698](https://docs.rs#698)        F: FnMut(&BindingInfo<'_>) -> R,
[699](https://docs.rs#699)        R: ToTokens,
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)        let pat = self.pat();
[702](https://docs.rs#702)        let mut body = TokenStream::new();
[703](https://docs.rs#703)        for binding in &self.bindings {
[704](https://docs.rs#704)            token::Brace::default().surround(&mut body, |body| {
[705](https://docs.rs#705)                f(binding).to_tokens(body);
[706](https://docs.rs#706)            });
[707](https://docs.rs#707)        }
[708](https://docs.rs#708)        quote!(#pat => { #body })
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    }
[710](https://docs.rs#710)
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// Runs the passed-in function once for each bound field, passing in the
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    /// result of the previous call, and a `BindingInfo`. generating a `match`
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    /// arm which evaluates to the resulting tokens.
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    ///
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    /// This method will ignore fields which are ignored through the `filter`
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// method.
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    ///
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    /// # Example
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    /// ```
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    ///     enum A {
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    ///         C(u32),
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    ///     }
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    /// };
[727](https://docs.rs#727)    /// let s = Structure::new(&di);
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    ///
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    /// assert_eq!(
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    ///     s.variants()[0].fold(quote!(0), |acc, bi| quote!(#acc + #bi)).to_string(),
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    ///
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    ///     quote!{
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    ///         A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,) => {
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    ///             0 + __binding_0 + __binding_1
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    ///         }
[736](https://docs.rs#736)    ///     }.to_string()
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    /// );
[738](https://docs.rs#738)    /// ```
[739](https://docs.rs#739)    pub fn fold<F, I, R>(&self, init: I, mut f: F) -> TokenStream
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    where
[741](https://docs.rs#741)        F: FnMut(TokenStream, &BindingInfo<'_>) -> R,
[742](https://docs.rs#742)        I: ToTokens,
[743](https://docs.rs#743)        R: ToTokens,
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    {
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        let pat = self.pat();
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        let body = self.bindings.iter().fold(quote!(#init), |i, bi| {
[747](https://docs.rs#747)            let r = f(i, bi);
[748](https://docs.rs#748)            quote!(#r)
[749](https://docs.rs#749)        });
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        quote!(#pat => { #body })
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    }
[752](https://docs.rs#752)
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    /// Filter the bindings created by this `Variant` object. This has 2 effects:
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    ///
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    /// * The bindings will no longer appear in match arms generated by methods
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    ///   on this `Variant` or its subobjects.
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    ///
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    /// * Impl blocks created with the `bound_impl` or `unsafe_bound_impl`
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    ///   method only consider type parameters referenced in the types of
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    ///   non-filtered fields.
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    ///
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    /// # Example
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    /// ```
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    ///     enum A {
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    ///         B{ a: i32, b: i32 },
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    ///         C{ a: u32 },
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    ///     }
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    /// };
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    ///
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    /// s.variants_mut()[0].filter(|bi| {
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    ///     bi.ast().ident == Some(quote::format_ident!("b"))
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    /// });
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    ///
[777](https://docs.rs#777)    /// assert_eq!(
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    ///     s.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[779](https://docs.rs#779)    ///
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    ///     quote!{
[781](https://docs.rs#781)    ///         A::B{ b: ref __binding_1, .. } => {
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_1) }
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    ///         }
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    ///         A::C{ a: ref __binding_0, } => {
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    ///         }
[787](https://docs.rs#787)    ///     }.to_string()
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    /// );
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    /// ```
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    pub fn filter<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> &mut Self
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    where
[792](https://docs.rs#792)        F: FnMut(&BindingInfo<'_>) -> bool,
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    {
[794](https://docs.rs#794)        self.bindings.retain(f);
[795](https://docs.rs#795)        self
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    }
[797](https://docs.rs#797)
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    /// Iterates all the bindings of this `Variant` object and uses a closure to determine if a
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    /// binding should be removed. If the closure returns `true` the binding is removed from the
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    /// variant. If the closure returns `false`, the binding remains in the variant.
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    ///
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    /// All the removed bindings are moved to a new `Variant` object which is otherwise identical
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    /// to the current one. To understand the effects of removing a binding from a variant check
[804](https://docs.rs#804)    /// the [`VariantInfo::filter`] documentation.
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    ///
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    /// # Example
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    /// ```
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    ///     enum A {
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    ///         B{ a: i32, b: i32 },
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    ///         C{ a: u32 },
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    ///     }
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    /// };
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    ///
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    /// let mut with_b = &mut s.variants_mut()[0];
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    ///
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    /// let with_a = with_b.drain_filter(|bi| {
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    ///     bi.ast().ident == Some(quote::format_ident!("a"))
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    /// });
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    ///
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    /// assert_eq!(
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    ///     with_a.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[825](https://docs.rs#825)    ///
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    ///     quote!{
[827](https://docs.rs#827)    ///         A::B{ a: ref __binding_0, .. } => {
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[829](https://docs.rs#829)    ///         }
[830](https://docs.rs#830)    ///     }.to_string()
[831](https://docs.rs#831)    /// );
[832](https://docs.rs#832)    ///
[833](https://docs.rs#833)    /// assert_eq!(
[834](https://docs.rs#834)    ///     with_b.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[835](https://docs.rs#835)    ///
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    ///     quote!{
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    ///         A::B{ b: ref __binding_1, .. } => {
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_1) }
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    ///         }
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    ///     }.to_string()
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    /// );
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    /// ```
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    #[allow(clippy::return_self_not_must_use)]
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    pub fn drain_filter<F>(&mut self, mut f: F) -> Self
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    where
[846](https://docs.rs#846)        F: FnMut(&BindingInfo<'_>) -> bool,
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    {
[848](https://docs.rs#848)        let mut other = VariantInfo {
[849](https://docs.rs#849)            prefix: self.prefix,
[850](https://docs.rs#850)            bindings: vec![],
[851](https://docs.rs#851)            ast: self.ast,
[852](https://docs.rs#852)            generics: self.generics,
[853](https://docs.rs#853)            original_length: self.original_length,
[854](https://docs.rs#854)        };
[855](https://docs.rs#855)
[856](https://docs.rs#856)        let (other_bindings, self_bindings) = self.bindings.drain(..).partition(&mut f);
[857](https://docs.rs#857)        other.bindings = other_bindings;
[858](https://docs.rs#858)        self.bindings = self_bindings;
[859](https://docs.rs#859)
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        other
[861](https://docs.rs#861)    }
[862](https://docs.rs#862)
[863](https://docs.rs#863)    /// Remove the binding at the given index.
[864](https://docs.rs#864)    ///
[865](https://docs.rs#865)    /// # Panics
[866](https://docs.rs#866)    ///
[867](https://docs.rs#867)    /// Panics if the index is out of range.
[868](https://docs.rs#868)    pub fn remove_binding(&mut self, idx: usize) -> &mut Self {
[869](https://docs.rs#869)        self.bindings.remove(idx);
[870](https://docs.rs#870)        self
[871](https://docs.rs#871)    }
[872](https://docs.rs#872)
[873](https://docs.rs#873)    /// Updates the `BindStyle` for each of the passed-in fields by calling the
[874](https://docs.rs#874)    /// passed-in function for each `BindingInfo`.
[875](https://docs.rs#875)    ///
[876](https://docs.rs#876)    /// # Example
[877](https://docs.rs#877)    /// ```
[878](https://docs.rs#878)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[879](https://docs.rs#879)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[880](https://docs.rs#880)    ///     enum A {
[881](https://docs.rs#881)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[882](https://docs.rs#882)    ///         C(u32),
[883](https://docs.rs#883)    ///     }
[884](https://docs.rs#884)    /// };
[885](https://docs.rs#885)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    ///
[887](https://docs.rs#887)    /// s.variants_mut()[0].bind_with(|bi| BindStyle::RefMut);
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    ///
[889](https://docs.rs#889)    /// assert_eq!(
[890](https://docs.rs#890)    ///     s.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[891](https://docs.rs#891)    ///
[892](https://docs.rs#892)    ///     quote!{
[893](https://docs.rs#893)    ///         A::B(ref mut __binding_0, ref mut __binding_1,) => {
[894](https://docs.rs#894)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[895](https://docs.rs#895)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_1) }
[896](https://docs.rs#896)    ///         }
[897](https://docs.rs#897)    ///         A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
[898](https://docs.rs#898)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[899](https://docs.rs#899)    ///         }
[900](https://docs.rs#900)    ///     }.to_string()
[901](https://docs.rs#901)    /// );
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    /// ```
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    pub fn bind_with<F>(&mut self, mut f: F) -> &mut Self
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    where
[905](https://docs.rs#905)        F: FnMut(&BindingInfo<'_>) -> BindStyle,
[906](https://docs.rs#906)    {
[907](https://docs.rs#907)        for binding in &mut self.bindings {
[908](https://docs.rs#908)            binding.style = f(binding);
[909](https://docs.rs#909)        }
[910](https://docs.rs#910)        self
[911](https://docs.rs#911)    }
[912](https://docs.rs#912)
[913](https://docs.rs#913)    /// Updates the binding name for each fo the passed-in fields by calling the
[914](https://docs.rs#914)    /// passed-in function for each `BindingInfo`.
[915](https://docs.rs#915)    ///
[916](https://docs.rs#916)    /// The function will be called with the `BindingInfo` and its index in the
[917](https://docs.rs#917)    /// enclosing variant.
[918](https://docs.rs#918)    ///
[919](https://docs.rs#919)    /// The default name is `__binding_{}` where `{}` is replaced with an
[920](https://docs.rs#920)    /// increasing number.
[921](https://docs.rs#921)    ///
[922](https://docs.rs#922)    /// # Example
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    /// ```
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    ///     enum A {
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    ///         B{ a: i32, b: i32 },
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    ///         C{ a: u32 },
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    ///     }
[930](https://docs.rs#930)    /// };
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    ///
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    /// s.variants_mut()[0].binding_name(|bi, i| bi.ident.clone().unwrap());
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    ///
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    /// assert_eq!(
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    ///     s.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    ///
[938](https://docs.rs#938)    ///     quote!{
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    ///         A::B{ a: ref a, b: ref b, } => {
[940](https://docs.rs#940)    ///             { println!("{:?}", a) }
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    ///             { println!("{:?}", b) }
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    ///         }
[943](https://docs.rs#943)    ///         A::C{ a: ref __binding_0, } => {
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[945](https://docs.rs#945)    ///         }
[946](https://docs.rs#946)    ///     }.to_string()
[947](https://docs.rs#947)    /// );
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    /// ```
[949](https://docs.rs#949)    pub fn binding_name<F>(&mut self, mut f: F) -> &mut Self
[950](https://docs.rs#950)    where
[951](https://docs.rs#951)        F: FnMut(&Field, usize) -> Ident,
[952](https://docs.rs#952)    {
[953](https://docs.rs#953)        for (it, binding) in self.bindings.iter_mut().enumerate() {
[954](https://docs.rs#954)            binding.binding = f(binding.field, it);
[955](https://docs.rs#955)        }
[956](https://docs.rs#956)        self
[957](https://docs.rs#957)    }
[958](https://docs.rs#958)
[959](https://docs.rs#959)    /// Returns a list of the type parameters which are referenced in this
[960](https://docs.rs#960)    /// field's type.
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    ///
[962](https://docs.rs#962)    /// # Caveat
[963](https://docs.rs#963)    ///
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    /// If the field contains any macros in type position, all parameters will
[965](https://docs.rs#965)    /// be considered bound. This is because we cannot determine which type
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    /// parameters are bound by type macros.
[967](https://docs.rs#967)    ///
[968](https://docs.rs#968)    /// # Example
[969](https://docs.rs#969)    /// ```
[970](https://docs.rs#970)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[971](https://docs.rs#971)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[972](https://docs.rs#972)    ///     struct A<T, U> {
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    ///         a: Option<T>,
[974](https://docs.rs#974)    ///         b: U,
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    ///     }
[976](https://docs.rs#976)    /// };
[977](https://docs.rs#977)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[978](https://docs.rs#978)    ///
[979](https://docs.rs#979)    /// assert_eq!(
[980](https://docs.rs#980)    ///     s.variants()[0].bindings()[0].referenced_ty_params(),
[981](https://docs.rs#981)    ///     &["e::format_ident!("T")]
[982](https://docs.rs#982)    /// );
[983](https://docs.rs#983)    /// ```
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    pub fn referenced_ty_params(&self) -> Vec<&'a Ident> {
[985](https://docs.rs#985)        let mut flags = Vec::new();
[986](https://docs.rs#986)        for binding in &self.bindings {
[987](https://docs.rs#987)            generics_fuse(&mut flags, &binding.seen_generics);
[988](https://docs.rs#988)        }
[989](https://docs.rs#989)        fetch_generics(&flags, self.generics)
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    }
[991](https://docs.rs#991)}
[992](https://docs.rs#992)
[993](https://docs.rs#993)/// A wrapper around a `syn::DeriveInput` which provides utilities for creating
[994](https://docs.rs#994)/// custom derive trait implementations.
[995](https://docs.rs#995)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[996](https://docs.rs#996)pub struct Structure<'a> {
[997](https://docs.rs#997)    variants: Vec<VariantInfo<'a>>,
[998](https://docs.rs#998)    omitted_variants: bool,
[999](https://docs.rs#999)    ast: &'a DeriveInput,
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)    extra_impl: Vec<GenericParam>,
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)    extra_predicates: Vec<WherePredicate>,
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)    add_bounds: AddBounds,
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)}
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)impl<'a> Structure<'a> {
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)    /// Create a new `Structure` with the variants and fields from the passed-in
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)    /// `DeriveInput`.
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)    ///
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)    /// # Panics
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)    ///
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)    /// This method will panic if the provided AST node represents an untagged
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)    /// union.
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)    pub fn new(ast: &'a DeriveInput) -> Self {
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)        Self::try_new(ast).expect("Unable to create synstructure::Structure")
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)    }
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)    /// Create a new `Structure` with the variants and fields from the passed-in
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)    /// `DeriveInput`.
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)    ///
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)    /// Unlike `Structure::new`, this method does not panic if the provided AST
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)    /// node represents an untagged union.
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)    pub fn try_new(ast: &'a DeriveInput) -> Result<Self> {
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)        let variants = match &ast.data {
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)            Data::Enum(data) => (&data.variants)
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)                .into_iter()
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)                .map(|v| {
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)                    VariantInfo::new(
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)                        VariantAst {
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)                            attrs: &v.attrs,
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)                            ident: &v.ident,
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)                            fields: &v.fields,
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)                            discriminant: &v.discriminant,
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)                        },
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)                        Some(&ast.ident),
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)                        &ast.generics,
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)                    )
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)                })
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)            Data::Struct(data) => {
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)                vec![VariantInfo::new(
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)                    VariantAst {
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)                        attrs: &ast.attrs,
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)                        ident: &ast.ident,
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)                        fields: &data.fields,
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)                        discriminant: &None,
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)                    },
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)                    None,
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)                    &ast.generics,
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)                )]
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)            }
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)            Data::Union(_) => {
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)                return Err(Error::new_spanned(
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)                    ast,
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)                    "unexpected unsupported untagged union",
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)                ));
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)            }
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)        };
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)        Ok(Structure {
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)            variants,
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)            omitted_variants: false,
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)            ast,
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)            extra_impl: vec![],
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)            extra_predicates: vec![],
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)            add_bounds: AddBounds::Both,
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)        })
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)    }
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)    /// Returns a slice of the variants in this Structure.
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)    pub fn variants(&self) -> &[VariantInfo<'a>] {
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)        &self.variants
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)    }
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)    /// Returns a mut slice of the variants in this Structure.
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)    pub fn variants_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [VariantInfo<'a>] {
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)        &mut self.variants
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)    }
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)    /// Returns a reference to the underlying `syn` AST node which this
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)    /// `Structure` was created from.
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)    pub fn ast(&self) -> &'a DeriveInput {
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)        self.ast
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)    }
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)    /// True if any variants were omitted due to a `filter_variants` call.
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)    pub fn omitted_variants(&self) -> bool {
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)        self.omitted_variants
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)    }
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)    /// Runs the passed-in function once for each bound field, passing in a `BindingInfo`.
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)    /// and generating `match` arms which evaluate the returned tokens.
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)    ///
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)    /// This method will ignore variants or fields which are ignored through the
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)    /// `filter` and `filter_variant` methods.
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)    ///
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)    /// # Example
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)    /// ```
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)    ///     enum A {
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)    ///         C(u32),
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)    ///     }
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)    /// };
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)    /// let s = Structure::new(&di);
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)    ///
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)    /// assert_eq!(
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)    ///     s.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)    ///
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)    ///     quote!{
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)    ///         A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,) => {
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_1) }
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)    ///         }
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)    ///         A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)    ///         }
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)    ///     }.to_string()
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)    /// );
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)    /// ```
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)    pub fn each<F, R>(&self, mut f: F) -> TokenStream
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)    where
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)        F: FnMut(&BindingInfo<'_>) -> R,
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)        R: ToTokens,
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)    {
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)        let mut t = TokenStream::new();
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)        for variant in &self.variants {
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)            variant.each(&mut f).to_tokens(&mut t);
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)        }
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)        if self.omitted_variants {
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)            quote!(_ => {}).to_tokens(&mut t);
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)        }
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)        t
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)    }
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)    /// Runs the passed-in function once for each bound field, passing in the
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)    /// result of the previous call, and a `BindingInfo`. generating `match`
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)    /// arms which evaluate to the resulting tokens.
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)    ///
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)    /// This method will ignore variants or fields which are ignored through the
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)    /// `filter` and `filter_variant` methods.
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)    ///
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)    /// If a variant has been ignored, it will return the `init` value.
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)    ///
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)    /// # Example
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)    /// ```
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)    ///     enum A {
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)    ///         C(u32),
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)    ///     }
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)    /// };
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)    /// let s = Structure::new(&di);
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)    ///
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)    /// assert_eq!(
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)    ///     s.fold(quote!(0), |acc, bi| quote!(#acc + #bi)).to_string(),
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)    ///
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)    ///     quote!{
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)    ///         A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,) => {
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)    ///             0 + __binding_0 + __binding_1
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)    ///         }
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)    ///         A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)    ///             0 + __binding_0
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)    ///         }
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)    ///     }.to_string()
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)    /// );
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)    /// ```
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)    pub fn fold<F, I, R>(&self, init: I, mut f: F) -> TokenStream
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)    where
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)        F: FnMut(TokenStream, &BindingInfo<'_>) -> R,
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)        I: ToTokens,
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)        R: ToTokens,
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)    {
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)        let mut t = TokenStream::new();
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)        for variant in &self.variants {
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)            variant.fold(&init, &mut f).to_tokens(&mut t);
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)        }
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)        if self.omitted_variants {
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)            quote!(_ => { #init }).to_tokens(&mut t);
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)        }
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)        t
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)    }
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)    /// Runs the passed-in function once for each variant, passing in a
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)    /// `VariantInfo`. and generating `match` arms which evaluate the returned
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)    /// tokens.
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)    ///
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)    /// This method will ignore variants and not bind fields which are ignored
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)    /// through the `filter` and `filter_variant` methods.
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)    ///
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)    /// # Example
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)    /// ```
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)    ///     enum A {
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)    ///         C(u32),
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)    ///     }
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)    /// };
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)    /// let s = Structure::new(&di);
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)    ///
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)    /// assert_eq!(
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)    ///     s.each_variant(|v| {
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)    ///         let name = &v.ast().ident;
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)    ///         quote!(println!(stringify!(#name)))
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)    ///     }).to_string(),
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)    ///
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)    ///     quote!{
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)    ///         A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,) => {
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)    ///             println!(stringify!(B))
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)    ///         }
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)    ///         A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)    ///             println!(stringify!(C))
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)    ///         }
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)    ///     }.to_string()
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)    /// );
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)    /// ```
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)    pub fn each_variant<F, R>(&self, mut f: F) -> TokenStream
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)    where
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)        F: FnMut(&VariantInfo<'_>) -> R,
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)        R: ToTokens,
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)    {
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)        let mut t = TokenStream::new();
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)        for variant in &self.variants {
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)            let pat = variant.pat();
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)            let body = f(variant);
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)            quote!(#pat => { #body }).to_tokens(&mut t);
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)        }
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)        if self.omitted_variants {
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)            quote!(_ => {}).to_tokens(&mut t);
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)        }
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)        t
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)    }
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)    /// Filter the bindings created by this `Structure` object. This has 2 effects:
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)    ///
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)    /// * The bindings will no longer appear in match arms generated by methods
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)    ///   on this `Structure` or its subobjects.
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)    ///
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)    /// * Impl blocks created with the `bound_impl` or `unsafe_bound_impl`
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)    ///   method only consider type parameters referenced in the types of
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)    ///   non-filtered fields.
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)    ///
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)    /// # Example
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)    /// ```
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)    ///     enum A {
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)    ///         B{ a: i32, b: i32 },
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)    ///         C{ a: u32 },
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)    ///     }
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)    /// };
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)    ///
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)    /// s.filter(|bi| {
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)    ///     bi.ast().ident == Some(quote::format_ident!("a"))
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)    /// });
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)    ///
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)    /// assert_eq!(
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)    ///     s.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)    ///
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)    ///     quote!{
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)    ///         A::B{ a: ref __binding_0, .. } => {
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)    ///         }
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)    ///         A::C{ a: ref __binding_0, } => {
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)    ///         }
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)    ///     }.to_string()
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    /// );
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)    /// ```
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)    pub fn filter<F>(&mut self, mut f: F) -> &mut Self
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)    where
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)        F: FnMut(&BindingInfo<'_>) -> bool,
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)    {
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)        for variant in &mut self.variants {
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)            variant.filter(&mut f);
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)        }
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)        self
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)    }
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)    /// Iterates all the bindings of this `Structure` object and uses a closure to determine if a
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)    /// binding should be removed. If the closure returns `true` the binding is removed from the
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)    /// structure. If the closure returns `false`, the binding remains in the structure.
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)    ///
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)    /// All the removed bindings are moved to a new `Structure` object which is otherwise identical
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)    /// to the current one. To understand the effects of removing a binding from a structure check
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)    /// the [`Structure::filter`] documentation.
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)    ///
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)    /// # Example
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)    /// ```
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)    ///     enum A {
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)    ///         B{ a: i32, b: i32 },
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)    ///         C{ a: u32 },
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)    ///     }
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)    /// };
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)    /// let mut with_b = Structure::new(&di);
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)    ///
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)    /// let with_a = with_b.drain_filter(|bi| {
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)    ///     bi.ast().ident == Some(quote::format_ident!("a"))
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)    /// });
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)    ///
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)    /// assert_eq!(
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)    ///     with_a.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)    ///
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)    ///     quote!{
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)    ///         A::B{ a: ref __binding_0, .. } => {
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)    ///         }
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)    ///         A::C{ a: ref __binding_0, } => {
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)    ///         }
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)    ///     }.to_string()
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)    /// );
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)    ///
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)    /// assert_eq!(
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)    ///     with_b.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)    ///
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)    ///     quote!{
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)    ///         A::B{ b: ref __binding_1, .. } => {
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_1) }
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)    ///         }
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)    ///         A::C{ .. } => {
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)    ///
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)    ///         }
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)    ///     }.to_string()
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)    /// );
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)    /// ```
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)    #[allow(clippy::return_self_not_must_use)]
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)    pub fn drain_filter<F>(&mut self, mut f: F) -> Self
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)    where
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)        F: FnMut(&BindingInfo<'_>) -> bool,
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)    {
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)        Self {
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)            variants: self
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)                .variants
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)                .iter_mut()
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)                .map(|variant| variant.drain_filter(&mut f))
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)                .collect(),
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)            omitted_variants: self.omitted_variants,
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)            ast: self.ast,
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)            extra_impl: self.extra_impl.clone(),
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)            extra_predicates: self.extra_predicates.clone(),
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)            add_bounds: self.add_bounds,
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)        }
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)    }
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)    /// Specify additional where predicate bounds which should be generated by
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)    /// impl-generating functions such as `gen_impl`, `bound_impl`, and
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)    /// `unsafe_bound_impl`.
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)    ///
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)    /// # Example
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)    /// ```
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)    ///         B(T),
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)    ///     }
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)    /// };
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)    ///
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)    /// // Add an additional where predicate.
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)    /// s.add_where_predicate(syn::parse_quote!(T: std::fmt::Display));
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)    ///
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)    /// assert_eq!(
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)    ///     s.bound_impl(quote!(krate::Trait), quote!{
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)    ///         fn a() {}
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)    ///     }).to_string(),
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)    ///     quote!{
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)    ///         const _: () = {
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)    ///             extern crate krate;
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)    ///             impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U>
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)    ///                 where T: std::fmt::Display,
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)    ///                       T: krate::Trait,
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)    ///                       Option<U>: krate::Trait,
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)    ///                       U: krate::Trait
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)    ///             {
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)    ///                 fn a() {}
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)    ///             }
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)    ///         };
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)    ///     }.to_string()
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)    /// );
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)    /// ```
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)    pub fn add_where_predicate(&mut self, pred: WherePredicate) -> &mut Self {
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)        self.extra_predicates.push(pred);
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)        self
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)    }
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)    /// Specify which bounds should be generated by impl-generating functions
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)    /// such as `gen_impl`, `bound_impl`, and `unsafe_bound_impl`.
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)    ///
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    /// The default behaviour is to generate both field and generic bounds from
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)    /// type parameters.
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)    ///
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)    /// # Example
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)    /// ```
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)    ///         B(T),
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)    ///     }
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)    /// };
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    ///
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)    /// // Limit bounds to only generics.
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    /// s.add_bounds(AddBounds::Generics);
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)    ///
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)    /// assert_eq!(
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)    ///     s.bound_impl(quote!(krate::Trait), quote!{
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)    ///         fn a() {}
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)    ///     }).to_string(),
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)    ///     quote!{
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)    ///         const _: () = {
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)    ///             extern crate krate;
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)    ///             impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U>
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)    ///                 where T: krate::Trait,
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)    ///                       U: krate::Trait
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)    ///             {
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)    ///                 fn a() {}
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)    ///             }
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)    ///         };
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)    ///     }.to_string()
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)    /// );
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)    /// ```
