[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)    pub fn add_bounds(&mut self, mode: AddBounds) -> &mut Self {
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)        self.add_bounds = mode;
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)        self
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)    }
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)    /// Filter the variants matched by this `Structure` object. This has 2 effects:
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)    ///
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)    /// * Match arms destructuring these variants will no longer be generated by
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)    ///   methods on this `Structure`
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)    ///
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)    /// * Impl blocks created with the `bound_impl` or `unsafe_bound_impl`
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)    ///   method only consider type parameters referenced in the types of
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)    ///   fields in non-fitered variants.
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)    ///
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)    /// # Example
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)    /// ```
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)    ///     enum A {
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)    ///         C(u32),
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)    ///     }
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)    /// };
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)    ///
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)    ///
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)    /// s.filter_variants(|v| v.ast().ident != "B");
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)    ///
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)    /// assert_eq!(
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)    ///     s.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)    ///
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)    ///     quote!{
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)    ///         A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)    ///         }
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)    ///         _ => {}
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)    ///     }.to_string()
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)    /// );
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)    /// ```
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)    pub fn filter_variants<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> &mut Self
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)    where
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)        F: FnMut(&VariantInfo<'_>) -> bool,
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)    {
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)        let before_len = self.variants.len();
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)        self.variants.retain(f);
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)        if self.variants.len() != before_len {
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)            self.omitted_variants = true;
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)        }
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)        self
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)    }
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)    /// Iterates all the variants of this `Structure` object and uses a closure to determine if a
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)    /// variant should be removed. If the closure returns `true` the variant is removed from the
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)    /// structure. If the closure returns `false`, the variant remains in the structure.
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)    ///
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)    /// All the removed variants are moved to a new `Structure` object which is otherwise identical
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)    /// to the current one. To understand the effects of removing a variant from a structure check
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)    /// the [`Structure::filter_variants`] documentation.
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)    ///
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)    /// # Example
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)    /// ```
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)    ///     enum A {
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)    ///         C(u32),
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)    ///     }
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)    /// };
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)    ///
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)    /// let mut with_c = Structure::new(&di);
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)    ///
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)    /// let with_b = with_c.drain_filter_variants(|v| v.ast().ident == "B");
[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)    ///
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)    /// assert_eq!(
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)    ///     with_c.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)    ///
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)    ///     quote!{
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)    ///         A::C(ref __binding_0,) => {
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)    ///         }
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)    ///     }.to_string()
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)    /// );
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)    ///
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)    /// assert_eq!(
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)    ///     with_b.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)    ///
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)    ///     quote!{
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)    ///         A::B(ref __binding_0, ref __binding_1,) => {
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_1) }
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)    ///         }
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)    ///     }.to_string()
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)    /// );
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)    #[allow(clippy::return_self_not_must_use)]
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)    pub fn drain_filter_variants<F>(&mut self, mut f: F) -> Self
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)    where
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)        F: FnMut(&VariantInfo<'_>) -> bool,
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)    {
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)        let mut other = Self {
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)            variants: vec![],
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)            omitted_variants: self.omitted_variants,
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)            ast: self.ast,
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)            extra_impl: self.extra_impl.clone(),
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)            extra_predicates: self.extra_predicates.clone(),
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)            add_bounds: self.add_bounds,
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)        };
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)        let (other_variants, self_variants) = self.variants.drain(..).partition(&mut f);
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)        other.variants = other_variants;
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)        self.variants = self_variants;
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)        other
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)    }
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)    /// Remove the variant at the given index.
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)    ///
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)    /// # Panics
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)    ///
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)    /// Panics if the index is out of range.
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)    pub fn remove_variant(&mut self, idx: usize) -> &mut Self {
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)        self.variants.remove(idx);
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)        self.omitted_variants = true;
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)        self
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)    }
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)    /// Updates the `BindStyle` for each of the passed-in fields by calling the
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)    /// passed-in function for each `BindingInfo`.
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)    ///
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)    /// # Example
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)    /// ```
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)    ///     enum A {
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)    ///         B(i32, i32),
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)    ///         C(u32),
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)    ///     }
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)    /// };
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)    ///
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)    /// s.bind_with(|bi| BindStyle::RefMut);
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)    ///
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)    /// assert_eq!(
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)    ///     s.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)    ///
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)    ///     quote!{
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)    ///         A::B(ref mut __binding_0, ref mut __binding_1,) => {
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_1) }
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)    ///         }
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)    ///         A::C(ref mut __binding_0,) => {
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)    ///             { println!("{:?}", __binding_0) }
[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)    ///         }
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)    ///     }.to_string()
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)    /// );
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)    /// ```
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)    pub fn bind_with<F>(&mut self, mut f: F) -> &mut Self
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)    where
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)        F: FnMut(&BindingInfo<'_>) -> BindStyle,
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)    {
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)        for variant in &mut self.variants {
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)            variant.bind_with(&mut f);
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)        }
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)        self
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)    }
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)    /// Updates the binding name for each fo the passed-in fields by calling the
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)    /// passed-in function for each `BindingInfo`.
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)    ///
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)    /// The function will be called with the `BindingInfo` and its index in the
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)    /// enclosing variant.
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)    ///
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)    /// The default name is `__binding_{}` where `{}` is replaced with an
[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)    /// increasing number.
[1602](https://docs.rs#1602)    ///
[1603](https://docs.rs#1603)    /// # Example
[1604](https://docs.rs#1604)    /// ```
[1605](https://docs.rs#1605)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)    ///     enum A {
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)    ///         B{ a: i32, b: i32 },
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)    ///         C{ a: u32 },
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)    ///     }
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)    /// };
[1612](https://docs.rs#1612)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1613](https://docs.rs#1613)    ///
[1614](https://docs.rs#1614)    /// s.binding_name(|bi, i| bi.ident.clone().unwrap());
[1615](https://docs.rs#1615)    ///
[1616](https://docs.rs#1616)    /// assert_eq!(
[1617](https://docs.rs#1617)    ///     s.each(|bi| quote!(println!("{:?}", #bi))).to_string(),
[1618](https://docs.rs#1618)    ///
[1619](https://docs.rs#1619)    ///     quote!{
[1620](https://docs.rs#1620)    ///         A::B{ a: ref a, b: ref b, } => {
[1621](https://docs.rs#1621)    ///             { println!("{:?}", a) }
[1622](https://docs.rs#1622)    ///             { println!("{:?}", b) }
[1623](https://docs.rs#1623)    ///         }
[1624](https://docs.rs#1624)    ///         A::C{ a: ref a, } => {
[1625](https://docs.rs#1625)    ///             { println!("{:?}", a) }
[1626](https://docs.rs#1626)    ///         }
[1627](https://docs.rs#1627)    ///     }.to_string()
[1628](https://docs.rs#1628)    /// );
[1629](https://docs.rs#1629)    /// ```
[1630](https://docs.rs#1630)    pub fn binding_name<F>(&mut self, mut f: F) -> &mut Self
[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)    where
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)        F: FnMut(&Field, usize) -> Ident,
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)    {
[1634](https://docs.rs#1634)        for variant in &mut self.variants {
[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)            variant.binding_name(&mut f);
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)        }
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)        self
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)    }
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)    /// Returns a list of the type parameters which are refrenced in the types
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)    /// of non-filtered fields / variants.
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)    ///
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)    /// # Caveat
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)    ///
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)    /// If the struct contains any macros in type position, all parameters will
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)    /// be considered bound. This is because we cannot determine which type
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)    /// parameters are bound by type macros.
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)    ///
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)    /// # Example
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)    /// ```
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)    ///         B(T, i32),
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)    ///     }
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)    /// };
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)    ///
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)    /// s.filter_variants(|v| v.ast().ident != "C");
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)    ///
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)    /// assert_eq!(
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)    ///     s.referenced_ty_params(),
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)    ///     &["e::format_ident!("T")]
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)    /// );
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)    /// ```
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)    pub fn referenced_ty_params(&self) -> Vec<&'a Ident> {
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)        let mut flags = Vec::new();
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)        for variant in &self.variants {
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)            for binding in &variant.bindings {
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)                generics_fuse(&mut flags, &binding.seen_generics);
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)            }
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)        }
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)        fetch_generics(&flags, &self.ast.generics)
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)    }
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)    /// Adds an `impl<>` generic parameter.
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)    /// This can be used when the trait to be derived needs some extra generic parameters.
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)    ///
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)    /// # Example
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)    /// ```
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)    ///         B(T),
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)    ///     }
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)    /// };
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)    /// let generic: syn::GenericParam = syn::parse_quote!(X: krate::AnotherTrait);
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)    ///
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)    /// assert_eq!(
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)    ///     s.add_impl_generic(generic)
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)    ///         .bound_impl(quote!(krate::Trait<X>),
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)    ///         quote!{
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)    ///                 fn a() {}
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)    ///         }
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)    ///     ).to_string(),
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)    ///     quote!{
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)    ///         const _: () = {
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)    ///             extern crate krate;
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)    ///             impl<T, U, X: krate::AnotherTrait> krate::Trait<X> for A<T, U>
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)    ///                 where T : krate :: Trait < X >,
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)    ///                       Option<U>: krate::Trait<X>,
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)    ///                       U: krate::Trait<X>
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)    ///             {
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)    ///                 fn a() {}
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)    ///             }
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)    ///         };
[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)    ///     }.to_string()
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)    /// );
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)    /// ```
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)    pub fn add_impl_generic(&mut self, param: GenericParam) -> &mut Self {
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)        self.extra_impl.push(param);
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)        self
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)    }
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)    /// Add trait bounds for a trait with the given path for each type parmaeter
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)    /// referenced in the types of non-filtered fields.
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)    ///
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)    /// # Caveat
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)    ///
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)    /// If the method contains any macros in type position, all parameters will
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)    /// be considered bound. This is because we cannot determine which type
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)    /// parameters are bound by type macros.
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)    pub fn add_trait_bounds(
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)        &self,
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)        bound: &TraitBound,
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)        where_clause: &mut Option<WhereClause>,
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)        mode: AddBounds,
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)    ) {
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)        // If we have any explicit where predicates, make sure to add them first.
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)        if !self.extra_predicates.is_empty() {
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)            let clause = get_or_insert_with(&mut *where_clause, || WhereClause {
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)                where_token: Default::default(),
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)                predicates: punctuated::Punctuated::new(),
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)            });
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)            clause
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)                .predicates
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)                .extend(self.extra_predicates.iter().cloned());
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)        }
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)        let mut seen = HashSet::new();
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)        let mut pred = |ty: Type| {
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)            if !seen.contains(&ty) {
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)                seen.insert(ty.clone());
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)                // Add a predicate.
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)                let clause = get_or_insert_with(&mut *where_clause, || WhereClause {
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)                    where_token: Default::default(),
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)                    predicates: punctuated::Punctuated::new(),
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)                });
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)                clause.predicates.push(WherePredicate::Type(PredicateType {
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)                    lifetimes: None,
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)                    bounded_ty: ty,
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)                    colon_token: Default::default(),
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)                    bounds: Some(punctuated::Pair::End(TypeParamBound::Trait(bound.clone())))
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)                        .into_iter()
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)                        .collect(),
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)                }));
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)            }
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)        };
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)        for variant in &self.variants {
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)            for binding in &variant.bindings {
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)                match mode {
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)                    AddBounds::Both | AddBounds::Fields => {
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)                        for &seen in &binding.seen_generics {
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)                            if seen {
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)                                pred(binding.ast().ty.clone());
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)                                break;
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)                            }
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)                        }
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)                    }
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)                    _ => {}
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)                }
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)                match mode {
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)                    AddBounds::Both | AddBounds::Generics => {
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)                        for param in binding.referenced_ty_params() {
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)                            pred(Type::Path(TypePath {
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)                                qself: None,
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)                                path: (*param).clone().into(),
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)                            }));
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)                        }
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)                    }
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)                    _ => {}
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)                }
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)            }
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)        }
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)    }
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)    /// This method is a no-op, underscore consts are used by default now.
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)    pub fn underscore_const(&mut self, _enabled: bool) -> &mut Self {
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)        self
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)    }
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)    /// > NOTE: This methods' features are superceded by `Structure::gen_impl`.
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)    ///
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)    /// Creates an `impl` block with the required generic type fields filled in
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)    /// to implement the trait `path`.
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)    ///
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)    /// This method also adds where clauses to the impl requiring that all
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)    /// referenced type parmaeters implement the trait `path`.
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)    ///
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)    /// # Hygiene and Paths
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)    ///
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)    /// This method wraps the impl block inside of a `const` (see the example
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)    /// below). In this scope, the first segment of the passed-in path is
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)    /// `extern crate`-ed in. If you don't want to generate that `extern crate`
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)    /// item, use a global path.
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)    ///
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)    /// This means that if you are implementing `my_crate::Trait`, you simply
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)    /// write `s.bound_impl(quote!(my_crate::Trait), quote!(...))`, and for the
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)    /// entirety of the definition, you can refer to your crate as `my_crate`.
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)    ///
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)    /// # Caveat
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)    ///
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)    /// If the method contains any macros in type position, all parameters will
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)    /// be considered bound. This is because we cannot determine which type
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)    /// parameters are bound by type macros.
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)    ///
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)    /// # Panics
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)    ///
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)    /// Panics if the path string parameter is not a valid `TraitBound`.
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)    ///
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)    /// # Example
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)    /// ```
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)    ///         B(T),
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)    ///     }
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)    /// };
[1836](https://docs.rs#1836)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1837](https://docs.rs#1837)    ///
[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)    /// s.filter_variants(|v| v.ast().ident != "B");
[1839](https://docs.rs#1839)    ///
[1840](https://docs.rs#1840)    /// assert_eq!(
[1841](https://docs.rs#1841)    ///     s.bound_impl(quote!(krate::Trait), quote!{
[1842](https://docs.rs#1842)    ///         fn a() {}
[1843](https://docs.rs#1843)    ///     }).to_string(),
[1844](https://docs.rs#1844)    ///     quote!{
[1845](https://docs.rs#1845)    ///         const _: () = {
[1846](https://docs.rs#1846)    ///             extern crate krate;
[1847](https://docs.rs#1847)    ///             impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U>
[1848](https://docs.rs#1848)    ///                 where Option<U>: krate::Trait,
[1849](https://docs.rs#1849)    ///                       U: krate::Trait
[1850](https://docs.rs#1850)    ///             {
[1851](https://docs.rs#1851)    ///                 fn a() {}
[1852](https://docs.rs#1852)    ///             }
[1853](https://docs.rs#1853)    ///         };
[1854](https://docs.rs#1854)    ///     }.to_string()
[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)    /// );
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)    /// ```
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)    pub fn bound_impl<P: ToTokens, B: ToTokens>(&self, path: P, body: B) -> TokenStream {
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)        self.impl_internal(
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)            path.into_token_stream(),
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)            body.into_token_stream(),
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)            quote!(),
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)            None,
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)        )
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)    }
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)    /// > NOTE: This methods' features are superceded by `Structure::gen_impl`.
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)    ///
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)    /// Creates an `impl` block with the required generic type fields filled in
[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)    /// to implement the unsafe trait `path`.
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)    ///
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)    /// This method also adds where clauses to the impl requiring that all
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)    /// referenced type parmaeters implement the trait `path`.
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)    ///
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)    /// # Hygiene and Paths
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)    ///
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)    /// This method wraps the impl block inside of a `const` (see the example
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)    /// below). In this scope, the first segment of the passed-in path is
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)    /// `extern crate`-ed in. If you don't want to generate that `extern crate`
[1879](https://docs.rs#1879)    /// item, use a global path.
[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)    ///
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)    /// This means that if you are implementing `my_crate::Trait`, you simply
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)    /// write `s.bound_impl(quote!(my_crate::Trait), quote!(...))`, and for the
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)    /// entirety of the definition, you can refer to your crate as `my_crate`.
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)    ///
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)    /// # Caveat
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)    ///
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)    /// If the method contains any macros in type position, all parameters will
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)    /// be considered bound. This is because we cannot determine which type
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)    /// parameters are bound by type macros.
[1890](https://docs.rs#1890)    ///
[1891](https://docs.rs#1891)    /// # Panics
[1892](https://docs.rs#1892)    ///
[1893](https://docs.rs#1893)    /// Panics if the path string parameter is not a valid `TraitBound`.
[1894](https://docs.rs#1894)    ///
[1895](https://docs.rs#1895)    /// # Example
[1896](https://docs.rs#1896)    /// ```
[1897](https://docs.rs#1897)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1898](https://docs.rs#1898)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1899](https://docs.rs#1899)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[1900](https://docs.rs#1900)    ///         B(T),
[1901](https://docs.rs#1901)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[1902](https://docs.rs#1902)    ///     }
[1903](https://docs.rs#1903)    /// };
[1904](https://docs.rs#1904)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1905](https://docs.rs#1905)    ///
[1906](https://docs.rs#1906)    /// s.filter_variants(|v| v.ast().ident != "B");
[1907](https://docs.rs#1907)    ///
[1908](https://docs.rs#1908)    /// assert_eq!(
[1909](https://docs.rs#1909)    ///     s.unsafe_bound_impl(quote!(krate::Trait), quote!{
[1910](https://docs.rs#1910)    ///         fn a() {}
[1911](https://docs.rs#1911)    ///     }).to_string(),
[1912](https://docs.rs#1912)    ///     quote!{
[1913](https://docs.rs#1913)    ///         const _: () = {
[1914](https://docs.rs#1914)    ///             extern crate krate;
[1915](https://docs.rs#1915)    ///             unsafe impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U>
[1916](https://docs.rs#1916)    ///                 where Option<U>: krate::Trait,
[1917](https://docs.rs#1917)    ///                       U: krate::Trait
[1918](https://docs.rs#1918)    ///             {
[1919](https://docs.rs#1919)    ///                 fn a() {}
[1920](https://docs.rs#1920)    ///             }
[1921](https://docs.rs#1921)    ///         };
[1922](https://docs.rs#1922)    ///     }.to_string()
[1923](https://docs.rs#1923)    /// );
[1924](https://docs.rs#1924)    /// ```
[1925](https://docs.rs#1925)    pub fn unsafe_bound_impl<P: ToTokens, B: ToTokens>(&self, path: P, body: B) -> TokenStream {
[1926](https://docs.rs#1926)        self.impl_internal(
[1927](https://docs.rs#1927)            path.into_token_stream(),
[1928](https://docs.rs#1928)            body.into_token_stream(),
[1929](https://docs.rs#1929)            quote!(unsafe),
[1930](https://docs.rs#1930)            None,
[1931](https://docs.rs#1931)        )
[1932](https://docs.rs#1932)    }
[1933](https://docs.rs#1933)
[1934](https://docs.rs#1934)    /// > NOTE: This methods' features are superceded by `Structure::gen_impl`.
[1935](https://docs.rs#1935)    ///
[1936](https://docs.rs#1936)    /// Creates an `impl` block with the required generic type fields filled in
[1937](https://docs.rs#1937)    /// to implement the trait `path`.
[1938](https://docs.rs#1938)    ///
[1939](https://docs.rs#1939)    /// This method will not add any where clauses to the impl.
[1940](https://docs.rs#1940)    ///
[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)    /// # Hygiene and Paths
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)    ///
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)    /// This method wraps the impl block inside of a `const` (see the example
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)    /// below). In this scope, the first segment of the passed-in path is
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)    /// `extern crate`-ed in. If you don't want to generate that `extern crate`
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)    /// item, use a global path.
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)    ///
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)    /// This means that if you are implementing `my_crate::Trait`, you simply
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)    /// write `s.bound_impl(quote!(my_crate::Trait), quote!(...))`, and for the
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)    /// entirety of the definition, you can refer to your crate as `my_crate`.
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)    ///
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)    /// # Panics
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)    ///
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)    /// Panics if the path string parameter is not a valid `TraitBound`.
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)    ///
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)    /// # Example
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)    /// ```
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)    ///         B(T),
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)    ///     }
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)    /// };
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)    ///
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)    /// s.filter_variants(|v| v.ast().ident != "B");
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)    ///
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)    /// assert_eq!(
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)    ///     s.unbound_impl(quote!(krate::Trait), quote!{
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)    ///         fn a() {}
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)    ///     }).to_string(),
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)    ///     quote!{
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)    ///         const _: () = {
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)    ///             extern crate krate;
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)    ///             impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U> {
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)    ///                 fn a() {}
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)    ///             }
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)    ///         };
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)    ///     }.to_string()
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)    /// );
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)    /// ```
[1983](https://docs.rs#1983)    pub fn unbound_impl<P: ToTokens, B: ToTokens>(&self, path: P, body: B) -> TokenStream {
[1984](https://docs.rs#1984)        self.impl_internal(
[1985](https://docs.rs#1985)            path.into_token_stream(),
[1986](https://docs.rs#1986)            body.into_token_stream(),
[1987](https://docs.rs#1987)            quote!(),
[1988](https://docs.rs#1988)            Some(AddBounds::None),
[1989](https://docs.rs#1989)        )
[1990](https://docs.rs#1990)    }
[1991](https://docs.rs#1991)
[1992](https://docs.rs#1992)    /// > NOTE: This methods' features are superceded by `Structure::gen_impl`.
[1993](https://docs.rs#1993)    ///
[1994](https://docs.rs#1994)    /// Creates an `impl` block with the required generic type fields filled in
[1995](https://docs.rs#1995)    /// to implement the unsafe trait `path`.
[1996](https://docs.rs#1996)    ///
[1997](https://docs.rs#1997)    /// This method will not add any where clauses to the impl.
[1998](https://docs.rs#1998)    ///
[1999](https://docs.rs#1999)    /// # Hygiene and Paths
[2000](https://docs.rs#2000)    ///
[2001](https://docs.rs#2001)    /// This method wraps the impl block inside of a `const` (see the example
[2002](https://docs.rs#2002)    /// below). In this scope, the first segment of the passed-in path is
[2003](https://docs.rs#2003)    /// `extern crate`-ed in. If you don't want to generate that `extern crate`
[2004](https://docs.rs#2004)    /// item, use a global path.
[2005](https://docs.rs#2005)    ///
[2006](https://docs.rs#2006)    /// This means that if you are implementing `my_crate::Trait`, you simply
[2007](https://docs.rs#2007)    /// write `s.bound_impl(quote!(my_crate::Trait), quote!(...))`, and for the
[2008](https://docs.rs#2008)    /// entirety of the definition, you can refer to your crate as `my_crate`.
[2009](https://docs.rs#2009)    ///
[2010](https://docs.rs#2010)    /// # Panics
[2011](https://docs.rs#2011)    ///
[2012](https://docs.rs#2012)    /// Panics if the path string parameter is not a valid `TraitBound`.
[2013](https://docs.rs#2013)    ///
[2014](https://docs.rs#2014)    /// # Example
[2015](https://docs.rs#2015)    /// ```
[2016](https://docs.rs#2016)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[2017](https://docs.rs#2017)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[2018](https://docs.rs#2018)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[2019](https://docs.rs#2019)    ///         B(T),
[2020](https://docs.rs#2020)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[2021](https://docs.rs#2021)    ///     }
[2022](https://docs.rs#2022)    /// };
[2023](https://docs.rs#2023)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[2024](https://docs.rs#2024)    ///
[2025](https://docs.rs#2025)    /// s.filter_variants(|v| v.ast().ident != "B");
[2026](https://docs.rs#2026)    ///
[2027](https://docs.rs#2027)    /// assert_eq!(
[2028](https://docs.rs#2028)    ///     s.unsafe_unbound_impl(quote!(krate::Trait), quote!{
[2029](https://docs.rs#2029)    ///         fn a() {}
[2030](https://docs.rs#2030)    ///     }).to_string(),
[2031](https://docs.rs#2031)    ///     quote!{
[2032](https://docs.rs#2032)    ///         const _: () = {
[2033](https://docs.rs#2033)    ///             extern crate krate;
[2034](https://docs.rs#2034)    ///             unsafe impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U> {
[2035](https://docs.rs#2035)    ///                 fn a() {}
[2036](https://docs.rs#2036)    ///             }
[2037](https://docs.rs#2037)    ///         };
[2038](https://docs.rs#2038)    ///     }.to_string()
[2039](https://docs.rs#2039)    /// );
[2040](https://docs.rs#2040)    /// ```
[2041](https://docs.rs#2041)    #[deprecated]
[2042](https://docs.rs#2042)    pub fn unsafe_unbound_impl<P: ToTokens, B: ToTokens>(&self, path: P, body: B) -> TokenStream {
[2043](https://docs.rs#2043)        self.impl_internal(
[2044](https://docs.rs#2044)            path.into_token_stream(),
[2045](https://docs.rs#2045)            body.into_token_stream(),
[2046](https://docs.rs#2046)            quote!(unsafe),
[2047](https://docs.rs#2047)            Some(AddBounds::None),
[2048](https://docs.rs#2048)        )
[2049](https://docs.rs#2049)    }
[2050](https://docs.rs#2050)
[2051](https://docs.rs#2051)    fn impl_internal(
[2052](https://docs.rs#2052)        &self,
[2053](https://docs.rs#2053)        path: TokenStream,
[2054](https://docs.rs#2054)        body: TokenStream,
[2055](https://docs.rs#2055)        safety: TokenStream,
[2056](https://docs.rs#2056)        mode: Option<AddBounds>,
[2057](https://docs.rs#2057)    ) -> TokenStream {
[2058](https://docs.rs#2058)        let mode = mode.unwrap_or(self.add_bounds);
[2059](https://docs.rs#2059)        let name = &self.ast.ident;
[2060](https://docs.rs#2060)        let mut gen_clone = self.ast.generics.clone();
[2061](https://docs.rs#2061)        gen_clone.params.extend(self.extra_impl.iter().cloned());
[2062](https://docs.rs#2062)        let (impl_generics, _, _) = gen_clone.split_for_impl();
[2063](https://docs.rs#2063)        let (_, ty_generics, where_clause) = self.ast.generics.split_for_impl();
[2064](https://docs.rs#2064)
[2065](https://docs.rs#2065)        let bound = syn::parse2::<TraitBound>(path)
[2066](https://docs.rs#2066)            .expect("`path` argument must be a valid rust trait bound");
[2067](https://docs.rs#2067)
[2068](https://docs.rs#2068)        let mut where_clause = where_clause.cloned();
[2069](https://docs.rs#2069)        self.add_trait_bounds(&bound, &mut where_clause, mode);
[2070](https://docs.rs#2070)
[2071](https://docs.rs#2071)        // This function is smart. If a global path is passed, no extern crate
[2072](https://docs.rs#2072)        // statement will be generated, however, a relative path will cause the
[2073](https://docs.rs#2073)        // crate which it is relative to to be imported within the current
[2074](https://docs.rs#2074)        // scope.
[2075](https://docs.rs#2075)        let mut extern_crate = quote!();
[2076](https://docs.rs#2076)        if bound.path.leading_colon.is_none() {
[2077](https://docs.rs#2077)            if let Some(seg) = bound.path.segments.first() {
[2078](https://docs.rs#2078)                let seg = &seg.ident;
[2079](https://docs.rs#2079)                extern_crate = quote! { extern crate #seg; };
[2080](https://docs.rs#2080)            }
[2081](https://docs.rs#2081)        }
[2082](https://docs.rs#2082)
[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)        let generated = quote! {
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)            #extern_crate
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)            #safety impl #impl_generics #bound for #name #ty_generics #where_clause {
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)                #body
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)            }
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)        };
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)        quote! {
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)            const _: () = { #generated };
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)        }
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)    }
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)
[2095](https://docs.rs#2095)    /// Generate an impl block for the given struct. This impl block will
[2096](https://docs.rs#2096)    /// automatically use hygiene tricks to avoid polluting the caller's
[2097](https://docs.rs#2097)    /// namespace, and will automatically add trait bounds for generic type
[2098](https://docs.rs#2098)    /// parameters.
[2099](https://docs.rs#2099)    ///
[2100](https://docs.rs#2100)    /// # Syntax
[2101](https://docs.rs#2101)    ///
[2102](https://docs.rs#2102)    /// This function accepts its arguments as a `TokenStream`. The recommended way
[2103](https://docs.rs#2103)    /// to call this function is passing the result of invoking the `quote!`
[2104](https://docs.rs#2104)    /// macro to it.
[2105](https://docs.rs#2105)    ///
[2106](https://docs.rs#2106)    /// ```ignore
[2107](https://docs.rs#2107)    /// s.gen_impl(quote! {
[2108](https://docs.rs#2108)    ///     // You can write any items which you want to import into scope here.
[2109](https://docs.rs#2109)    ///     // For example, you may want to include an `extern crate` for the
[2110](https://docs.rs#2110)    ///     // crate which implements your trait. These items will only be
[2111](https://docs.rs#2111)    ///     // visible to the code you generate, and won't be exposed to the
[2112](https://docs.rs#2112)    ///     // consuming crate
[2113](https://docs.rs#2113)    ///     extern crate krate;
[2114](https://docs.rs#2114)    ///
[2115](https://docs.rs#2115)    ///     // You can also add `use` statements here to bring types or traits
[2116](https://docs.rs#2116)    ///     // into scope.
[2117](https://docs.rs#2117)    ///     //
[2118](https://docs.rs#2118)    ///     // WARNING: Try not to use common names here, because the stable
[2119](https://docs.rs#2119)    ///     // version of syn does not support hygiene and you could accidentally
[2120](https://docs.rs#2120)    ///     // shadow types from the caller crate.
[2121](https://docs.rs#2121)    ///     use krate::Trait as MyTrait;
[2122](https://docs.rs#2122)    ///
[2123](https://docs.rs#2123)    ///     // The actual impl block is a `gen impl` or `gen unsafe impl` block.
[2124](https://docs.rs#2124)    ///     // You can use `@Self` to refer to the structure's type.
[2125](https://docs.rs#2125)    ///     gen impl MyTrait for @Self {
[2126](https://docs.rs#2126)    ///         fn f(&self) { ... }
[2127](https://docs.rs#2127)    ///     }
[2128](https://docs.rs#2128)    /// })
[2129](https://docs.rs#2129)    /// ```
[2130](https://docs.rs#2130)    ///
[2131](https://docs.rs#2131)    /// The most common usage of this trait involves loading the crate the
[2132](https://docs.rs#2132)    /// target trait comes from with `extern crate`, and then invoking a `gen
[2133](https://docs.rs#2133)    /// impl` block.
[2134](https://docs.rs#2134)    ///
[2135](https://docs.rs#2135)    /// # Hygiene
[2136](https://docs.rs#2136)    ///
[2137](https://docs.rs#2137)    /// This method tries to handle hygiene intelligently for both stable and
[2138](https://docs.rs#2138)    /// unstable proc-macro implementations, however there are visible
[2139](https://docs.rs#2139)    /// differences.
[2140](https://docs.rs#2140)    ///
[2141](https://docs.rs#2141)    /// The output of every `gen_impl` function is wrapped in a dummy `const`
[2142](https://docs.rs#2142)    /// value, to ensure that it is given its own scope, and any values brought
[2143](https://docs.rs#2143)    /// into scope are not leaked to the calling crate.
[2144](https://docs.rs#2144)    ///
[2145](https://docs.rs#2145)    /// By default, the above invocation may generate an output like the
[2146](https://docs.rs#2146)    /// following:
[2147](https://docs.rs#2147)    ///
[2148](https://docs.rs#2148)    /// ```ignore
[2149](https://docs.rs#2149)    /// const _: () = {
[2150](https://docs.rs#2150)    ///     extern crate krate;
[2151](https://docs.rs#2151)    ///     use krate::Trait as MyTrait;
[2152](https://docs.rs#2152)    ///     impl<T> MyTrait for Struct<T> where T: MyTrait {
[2153](https://docs.rs#2153)    ///         fn f(&self) { ... }
[2154](https://docs.rs#2154)    ///     }
[2155](https://docs.rs#2155)    /// };
[2156](https://docs.rs#2156)    /// ```
[2157](https://docs.rs#2157)    ///
[2158](https://docs.rs#2158)    /// ### Using the `std` crate
[2159](https://docs.rs#2159)    ///
[2160](https://docs.rs#2160)    /// If you are using `quote!()` to implement your trait, with the
[2161](https://docs.rs#2161)    /// `proc-macro2/nightly` feature, `std` isn't considered to be in scope for
[2162](https://docs.rs#2162)    /// your macro. This means that if you use types from `std` in your
[2163](https://docs.rs#2163)    /// procedural macro, you'll want to explicitly load it with an `extern
[2164](https://docs.rs#2164)    /// crate std;`.
[2165](https://docs.rs#2165)    ///
[2166](https://docs.rs#2166)    /// ### Absolute paths
[2167](https://docs.rs#2167)    ///
[2168](https://docs.rs#2168)    /// You should generally avoid using absolute paths in your generated code,
[2169](https://docs.rs#2169)    /// as they will resolve very differently when using the stable and nightly
[2170](https://docs.rs#2170)    /// versions of `proc-macro2`. Instead, load the crates you need to use
[2171](https://docs.rs#2171)    /// explictly with `extern crate` and
[2172](https://docs.rs#2172)    ///
[2173](https://docs.rs#2173)    /// # Trait Bounds
[2174](https://docs.rs#2174)    ///
[2175](https://docs.rs#2175)    /// This method will automatically add trait bounds for any type parameters
[2176](https://docs.rs#2176)    /// which are referenced within the types of non-ignored fields.
[2177](https://docs.rs#2177)    ///
[2178](https://docs.rs#2178)    /// Additional type parameters may be added with the generics syntax after
[2179](https://docs.rs#2179)    /// the `impl` keyword.
[2180](https://docs.rs#2180)    ///
[2181](https://docs.rs#2181)    /// ### Type Macro Caveat
[2182](https://docs.rs#2182)    ///
[2183](https://docs.rs#2183)    /// If the method contains any macros in type position, all parameters will
[2184](https://docs.rs#2184)    /// be considered bound. This is because we cannot determine which type
[2185](https://docs.rs#2185)    /// parameters are bound by type macros.
[2186](https://docs.rs#2186)    ///
[2187](https://docs.rs#2187)    /// # Errors
[2188](https://docs.rs#2188)    ///
[2189](https://docs.rs#2189)    /// This function will generate a `compile_error!` if additional type
[2190](https://docs.rs#2190)    /// parameters added by `impl<..>` conflict with generic type parameters on
[2191](https://docs.rs#2191)    /// the original struct.
[2192](https://docs.rs#2192)    ///
[2193](https://docs.rs#2193)    /// # Panics
[2194](https://docs.rs#2194)    ///
[2195](https://docs.rs#2195)    /// This function will panic if the input `TokenStream` is not well-formed.
[2196](https://docs.rs#2196)    ///
[2197](https://docs.rs#2197)    /// # Example Usage
[2198](https://docs.rs#2198)    ///
[2199](https://docs.rs#2199)    /// ```
[2200](https://docs.rs#2200)    /// # use synstructure::*;
[2201](https://docs.rs#2201)    /// let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
[2202](https://docs.rs#2202)    ///     enum A<T, U> {
[2203](https://docs.rs#2203)    ///         B(T),
[2204](https://docs.rs#2204)    ///         C(Option<U>),
[2205](https://docs.rs#2205)    ///     }
[2206](https://docs.rs#2206)    /// };
[2207](https://docs.rs#2207)    /// let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
[2208](https://docs.rs#2208)    ///
[2209](https://docs.rs#2209)    /// s.filter_variants(|v| v.ast().ident != "B");
[2210](https://docs.rs#2210)    ///
[2211](https://docs.rs#2211)    /// assert_eq!(
[2212](https://docs.rs#2212)    ///     s.gen_impl(quote! {
[2213](https://docs.rs#2213)    ///         extern crate krate;
[2214](https://docs.rs#2214)    ///         gen impl krate::Trait for @Self {
[2215](https://docs.rs#2215)    ///             fn a() {}
[2216](https://docs.rs#2216)    ///         }
[2217](https://docs.rs#2217)    ///     }).to_string(),
[2218](https://docs.rs#2218)    ///     quote!{
[2219](https://docs.rs#2219)    ///         const _: () = {
[2220](https://docs.rs#2220)    ///             extern crate krate;
[2221](https://docs.rs#2221)    ///             impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U>
[2222](https://docs.rs#2222)    ///             where
[2223](https://docs.rs#2223)    ///                 Option<U>: krate::Trait,
[2224](https://docs.rs#2224)    ///                 U: krate::Trait
[2225](https://docs.rs#2225)    ///             {
[2226](https://docs.rs#2226)    ///                 fn a() {}
[2227](https://docs.rs#2227)    ///             }
[2228](https://docs.rs#2228)    ///         };
[2229](https://docs.rs#2229)    ///     }.to_string()
[2230](https://docs.rs#2230)    /// );
[2231](https://docs.rs#2231)    ///
[2232](https://docs.rs#2232)    /// // NOTE: You can also add extra generics after the impl
[2233](https://docs.rs#2233)    /// assert_eq!(
[2234](https://docs.rs#2234)    ///     s.gen_impl(quote! {
[2235](https://docs.rs#2235)    ///         extern crate krate;
[2236](https://docs.rs#2236)    ///         gen impl<X: krate::OtherTrait> krate::Trait<X> for @Self
[2237](https://docs.rs#2237)    ///         where
[2238](https://docs.rs#2238)    ///             X: Send + Sync,
[2239](https://docs.rs#2239)    ///         {
[2240](https://docs.rs#2240)    ///             fn a() {}
[2241](https://docs.rs#2241)    ///         }
[2242](https://docs.rs#2242)    ///     }).to_string(),
[2243](https://docs.rs#2243)    ///     quote!{
[2244](https://docs.rs#2244)    ///         const _: () = {
[2245](https://docs.rs#2245)    ///             extern crate krate;
[2246](https://docs.rs#2246)    ///             impl<X: krate::OtherTrait, T, U> krate::Trait<X> for A<T, U>
[2247](https://docs.rs#2247)    ///             where
[2248](https://docs.rs#2248)    ///                 X: Send + Sync,
[2249](https://docs.rs#2249)    ///                 Option<U>: krate::Trait<X>,
[2250](https://docs.rs#2250)    ///                 U: krate::Trait<X>
[2251](https://docs.rs#2251)    ///             {
[2252](https://docs.rs#2252)    ///                 fn a() {}
[2253](https://docs.rs#2253)    ///             }
[2254](https://docs.rs#2254)    ///         };
[2255](https://docs.rs#2255)    ///     }.to_string()
[2256](https://docs.rs#2256)    /// );
[2257](https://docs.rs#2257)    ///
[2258](https://docs.rs#2258)    /// // NOTE: you can generate multiple traits with a single call
[2259](https://docs.rs#2259)    /// assert_eq!(
[2260](https://docs.rs#2260)    ///     s.gen_impl(quote! {
[2261](https://docs.rs#2261)    ///         extern crate krate;
[2262](https://docs.rs#2262)    ///
[2263](https://docs.rs#2263)    ///         gen impl krate::Trait for @Self {
[2264](https://docs.rs#2264)    ///             fn a() {}
[2265](https://docs.rs#2265)    ///         }
[2266](https://docs.rs#2266)    ///
[2267](https://docs.rs#2267)    ///         gen impl krate::OtherTrait for @Self {
[2268](https://docs.rs#2268)    ///             fn b() {}
[2269](https://docs.rs#2269)    ///         }
[2270](https://docs.rs#2270)    ///     }).to_string(),
[2271](https://docs.rs#2271)    ///     quote!{
[2272](https://docs.rs#2272)    ///         const _: () = {
[2273](https://docs.rs#2273)    ///             extern crate krate;
[2274](https://docs.rs#2274)    ///             impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U>
[2275](https://docs.rs#2275)    ///             where
[2276](https://docs.rs#2276)    ///                 Option<U>: krate::Trait,
[2277](https://docs.rs#2277)    ///                 U: krate::Trait
[2278](https://docs.rs#2278)    ///             {
[2279](https://docs.rs#2279)    ///                 fn a() {}
[2280](https://docs.rs#2280)    ///             }
[2281](https://docs.rs#2281)    ///
[2282](https://docs.rs#2282)    ///             impl<T, U> krate::OtherTrait for A<T, U>
[2283](https://docs.rs#2283)    ///             where
[2284](https://docs.rs#2284)    ///                 Option<U>: krate::OtherTrait,
[2285](https://docs.rs#2285)    ///                 U: krate::OtherTrait
[2286](https://docs.rs#2286)    ///             {
[2287](https://docs.rs#2287)    ///                 fn b() {}
[2288](https://docs.rs#2288)    ///             }
[2289](https://docs.rs#2289)    ///         };
[2290](https://docs.rs#2290)    ///     }.to_string()
[2291](https://docs.rs#2291)    /// );
[2292](https://docs.rs#2292)    /// ```
[2293](https://docs.rs#2293)    ///
[2294](https://docs.rs#2294)    /// Use `add_bounds` to change which bounds are generated.
[2295](https://docs.rs#2295)    pub fn gen_impl(&self, cfg: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[2296](https://docs.rs#2296)        Parser::parse2(
[2297](https://docs.rs#2297)            |input: ParseStream<'_>| -> Result<TokenStream> { self.gen_impl_parse(input, true) },
[2298](https://docs.rs#2298)            cfg,
[2299](https://docs.rs#2299)        )
[2300](https://docs.rs#2300)        .expect("Failed to parse gen_impl")
[2301](https://docs.rs#2301)    }
[2302](https://docs.rs#2302)
[2303](https://docs.rs#2303)    fn gen_impl_parse(&self, input: ParseStream<'_>, wrap: bool) -> Result<TokenStream> {
[2304](https://docs.rs#2304)        fn parse_prefix(input: ParseStream<'_>) -> Result<Option<Token![unsafe]>> {
[2305](https://docs.rs#2305)            if input.parse::<Ident>()? != "gen" {
[2306](https://docs.rs#2306)                return Err(input.error("Expected keyword `gen`"));
[2307](https://docs.rs#2307)            }
[2308](https://docs.rs#2308)            let safety = input.parse::<Option<Token![unsafe]>>()?;
[2309](https://docs.rs#2309)            let _ = input.parse::<Token![impl]>()?;
[2310](https://docs.rs#2310)            Ok(safety)
[2311](https://docs.rs#2311)        }
[2312](https://docs.rs#2312)
[2313](https://docs.rs#2313)        let mut before = vec![];
[2314](https://docs.rs#2314)        loop {
[2315](https://docs.rs#2315)            if parse_prefix(&input.fork()).is_ok() {
[2316](https://docs.rs#2316)                break;
[2317](https://docs.rs#2317)            }
[2318](https://docs.rs#2318)            before.push(input.parse::<TokenTree>()?);
[2319](https://docs.rs#2319)        }
[2320](https://docs.rs#2320)
[2321](https://docs.rs#2321)        // Parse the prefix "for real"
[2322](https://docs.rs#2322)        let safety = parse_prefix(input)?;
[2323](https://docs.rs#2323)
[2324](https://docs.rs#2324)        // optional `<>`
[2325](https://docs.rs#2325)        let mut generics = input.parse::<Generics>()?;
[2326](https://docs.rs#2326)
[2327](https://docs.rs#2327)        // @bound
[2328](https://docs.rs#2328)        let bound = input.parse::<TraitBound>()?;
[2329](https://docs.rs#2329)
[2330](https://docs.rs#2330)        // `for @Self`
[2331](https://docs.rs#2331)        let _ = input.parse::<Token![for]>()?;
[2332](https://docs.rs#2332)        let _ = input.parse::<Token![@]>()?;
[2333](https://docs.rs#2333)        let _ = input.parse::<Token![Self]>()?;
[2334](https://docs.rs#2334)
[2335](https://docs.rs#2335)        // optional `where ...`
[2336](https://docs.rs#2336)        generics.where_clause = input.parse()?;
[2337](https://docs.rs#2337)
[2338](https://docs.rs#2338)        // Body of the impl
[2339](https://docs.rs#2339)        let body;
[2340](https://docs.rs#2340)        braced!(body in input);
[2341](https://docs.rs#2341)        let body = body.parse::<TokenStream>()?;
[2342](https://docs.rs#2342)
[2343](https://docs.rs#2343)        // Try to parse the next entry in sequence. If this fails, we'll fall
[2344](https://docs.rs#2344)        // back to just parsing the entire rest of the TokenStream.
[2345](https://docs.rs#2345)        let maybe_next_impl = self.gen_impl_parse(&input.fork(), false);
[2346](https://docs.rs#2346)
[2347](https://docs.rs#2347)        // Eat tokens to the end. Whether or not our speculative nested parse
[2348](https://docs.rs#2348)        // succeeded, we're going to want to consume the rest of our input.
[2349](https://docs.rs#2349)        let mut after = input.parse::<TokenStream>()?;
[2350](https://docs.rs#2350)        if let Ok(stream) = maybe_next_impl {
[2351](https://docs.rs#2351)            after = stream;
[2352](https://docs.rs#2352)        }
[2353](https://docs.rs#2353)        assert!(input.is_empty(), "Should've consumed the rest of our input");
[2354](https://docs.rs#2354)
[2355](https://docs.rs#2355)        /* Codegen Logic */
[2356](https://docs.rs#2356)        let name = &self.ast.ident;
[2357](https://docs.rs#2357)
[2358](https://docs.rs#2358)        // Add the generics from the original struct in, and then add any
[2359](https://docs.rs#2359)        // additional trait bounds which we need on the type.
[2360](https://docs.rs#2360)        if let Err(err) = merge_generics(&mut generics, &self.ast.generics) {
[2361](https://docs.rs#2361)            // Report the merge error as a `compile_error!`, as it may be
[2362](https://docs.rs#2362)            // triggerable by an end-user.
[2363](https://docs.rs#2363)            return Ok(err.to_compile_error());
[2364](https://docs.rs#2364)        }
[2365](https://docs.rs#2365)
[2366](https://docs.rs#2366)        self.add_trait_bounds(&bound, &mut generics.where_clause, self.add_bounds);
[2367](https://docs.rs#2367)        let (impl_generics, _, where_clause) = generics.split_for_impl();
[2368](https://docs.rs#2368)        let (_, ty_generics, _) = self.ast.generics.split_for_impl();
[2369](https://docs.rs#2369)
[2370](https://docs.rs#2370)        let generated = quote! {
[2371](https://docs.rs#2371)            #(#before)*
[2372](https://docs.rs#2372)            #safety impl #impl_generics #bound for #name #ty_generics #where_clause {
[2373](https://docs.rs#2373)                #body
[2374](https://docs.rs#2374)            }
[2375](https://docs.rs#2375)            #after
[2376](https://docs.rs#2376)        };
[2377](https://docs.rs#2377)
[2378](https://docs.rs#2378)        if wrap {
[2379](https://docs.rs#2379)            Ok(quote! {
[2380](https://docs.rs#2380)                const _: () = { #generated };
[2381](https://docs.rs#2381)            })
[2382](https://docs.rs#2382)        } else {
[2383](https://docs.rs#2383)            Ok(generated)
[2384](https://docs.rs#2384)        }
[2385](https://docs.rs#2385)    }
[2386](https://docs.rs#2386)}
[2387](https://docs.rs#2387)
[2388](https://docs.rs#2388)/// Dumps an unpretty version of a tokenstream. Takes any type which implements
[2389](https://docs.rs#2389)/// `Display`.
[2390](https://docs.rs#2390)///
[2391](https://docs.rs#2391)/// This is mostly useful for visualizing the output of a procedural macro, as
[2392](https://docs.rs#2392)/// it makes it marginally more readable. It is used in the implementation of
[2393](https://docs.rs#2393)/// `test_derive!` to unprettily print the output.
[2394](https://docs.rs#2394)///
[2395](https://docs.rs#2395)/// # Stability
[2396](https://docs.rs#2396)///
[2397](https://docs.rs#2397)/// The stability of the output of this function is not guaranteed. Do not
[2398](https://docs.rs#2398)/// assert that the output of this function does not change between minor
[2399](https://docs.rs#2399)/// versions.
[2400](https://docs.rs#2400)///
[2401](https://docs.rs#2401)/// # Example
[2402](https://docs.rs#2402)///
[2403](https://docs.rs#2403)/// ```
[2404](https://docs.rs#2404)/// # use quote::quote;
[2405](https://docs.rs#2405)/// assert_eq!(
[2406](https://docs.rs#2406)///     synstructure::unpretty_print(quote! {
[2407](https://docs.rs#2407)///         const _: () = {
[2408](https://docs.rs#2408)///             extern crate krate;
[2409](https://docs.rs#2409)///             impl<T, U> krate::Trait for A<T, U>
[2410](https://docs.rs#2410)///             where
[2411](https://docs.rs#2411)///                 Option<U>: krate::Trait,
[2412](https://docs.rs#2412)///                 U: krate::Trait
[2413](https://docs.rs#2413)///             {
[2414](https://docs.rs#2414)///                 fn a() {}
[2415](https://docs.rs#2415)///             }
[2416](https://docs.rs#2416)///         };
[2417](https://docs.rs#2417)///     }),
[2418](https://docs.rs#2418)///     "const _ : (
[2419](https://docs.rs#2419)///     )
[2420](https://docs.rs#2420)/// = {
[2421](https://docs.rs#2421)///     extern crate krate ;
[2422](https://docs.rs#2422)///     impl < T , U > krate :: Trait for A < T , U > where Option < U > : krate :: Trait , U : krate :: Trait {
[2423](https://docs.rs#2423)///         fn a (
[2424](https://docs.rs#2424)///             )
[2425](https://docs.rs#2425)///         {
[2426](https://docs.rs#2426)///             }
[2427](https://docs.rs#2427)///         }
[2428](https://docs.rs#2428)///     }
[2429](https://docs.rs#2429)/// ;
[2430](https://docs.rs#2430)/// "
[2431](https://docs.rs#2431)/// )
[2432](https://docs.rs#2432)/// ```
[2433](https://docs.rs#2433)pub fn unpretty_print<T: std::fmt::Display>(ts: T) -> String {
[2434](https://docs.rs#2434)    let mut res = String::new();
[2435](https://docs.rs#2435)
[2436](https://docs.rs#2436)    let raw_s = ts.to_string();
[2437](https://docs.rs#2437)    let mut s = &raw_s[..];
[2438](https://docs.rs#2438)    let mut indent = 0;
[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)    while let Some(i) = s.find(&['(', '{', '[', ')', '}', ']', ';'][..]) {
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)        match &s[i..=i] {
[2441](https://docs.rs#2441)            "(" | "{" | "[" => indent += 1,
[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)            ")" | "}" | "]" => indent -= 1,
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)            _ => {}
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)        }
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)        res.push_str(&s[..=i]);
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)        res.push('\n');
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)        for _ in 0..indent {
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)            res.push_str("    ");
[2449](https://docs.rs#2449)        }
[2450](https://docs.rs#2450)        s = trim_start_matches(&s[i + 1..], ' ');
[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)    }
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)    res.push_str(s);
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)    res
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)}
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)/// `trim_left_matches` has been deprecated in favor of `trim_start_matches`.

# decl_attribute in synstructure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/synstructure/0.13.2/synstructure/macro.decl_attribute.html

```
macro_rules! decl_attribute {
    ([$attribute:ident] => $(#[$($attrs:tt)*])* $inner:path) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

The `decl_attribute!` macro declares a custom attribute wrapper. It will
parse the incoming `TokenStream` into a `synstructure::Structure` object,
and pass it into the inner function.

Your inner function should have the following type:

```
fn attribute(
    attr: proc_macro2::TokenStream,
    structure: synstructure::Structure,
) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    unimplemented!()
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
fn attribute_interesting(
    _attr: proc_macro2::TokenStream,
    _structure: synstructure::Structure,
) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    quote::quote! { ... }
}
decl_attribute!([interesting] => attribute_interesting);
```
*This macro is available if  synstructure is built with the "proc-macro"
feature.*

---

# decl_derive in synstructure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/synstructure/0.13.2/synstructure/macro.decl_derive.html

```
macro_rules! decl_derive {
    ([$derives:ident $($derive_t:tt)*] => $(#[$($attrs:tt)*])* $inner:path) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

The `decl_derive!` macro declares a custom derive wrapper. It will parse the
incoming `TokenStream` into a `synstructure::Structure` object, and pass it
into the inner function.

Your inner function should take a `synstructure::Structure` by value, and
return a type implementing `synstructure::MacroResult`, for example:

```
fn derive_simple(input: synstructure::Structure) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    unimplemented!()
}
fn derive_result(input: synstructure::Structure)
    -> syn::Result<proc_macro2::TokenStream>
{
    unimplemented!()
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#without-attributes)Without Attributes

```
fn derive_interesting(_input: synstructure::Structure) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    quote::quote! { ... }
}
decl_derive!([Interesting] => derive_interesting);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#with-attributes)With Attributes

```
fn derive_interesting(_input: synstructure::Structure) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    quote::quote! { ... }
}
decl_derive!([Interesting, attributes(interesting_ignore)] => derive_interesting);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#decl-attributes--doc-comments)Decl Attributes & Doc Comments

```
fn derive_interesting(_input: synstructure::Structure) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    quote::quote! { ... }
}
decl_derive! {
    [Interesting] =>
    #[allow(some_lint)]
    /// Documentation Comments
    derive_interesting
}
```
*This macro is available if  synstructure is built with the "proc-macro"
feature.*

---

# test_derive in synstructure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/synstructure/0.13.2/synstructure/macro.test_derive.html

```
macro_rules! test_derive {
    ($name:path { $($i:tt)* } expands to { $($o:tt)* }) => { ... };
    ($name:path { $($i:tt)* } expands to { $($o:tt)* } no_build) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Run a test on a custom derive. This macro expands both the original struct and the expansion to ensure that they compile correctly, and confirms that feeding the original struct into the named derive will produce the written output.

You can add `no_build` to the end of the macro invocation to disable
checking that the written code compiles. This is useful in contexts where
the procedural macro cannot depend on the crate where it is used during
tests.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
fn test_derive_example(_s: synstructure::Structure)
    -> Result<proc_macro2::TokenStream, syn::Error>
{
    Ok(quote::quote! { const YOUR_OUTPUT: &'static str = "here"; })
}
fn main() {
    synstructure::test_derive!{
        test_derive_example {
            struct A;
        }
        expands to {
            const YOUR_OUTPUT: &'static str = "here";
        }
    }
}
```

# BindingInfo in synstructure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/synstructure/0.13.2/synstructure/struct.BindingInfo.html

## Expand description

Information about a specific binding. This contains both an `Ident`
reference to the given field, and the syn `&'a Field` descriptor for that
field.

This type supports `quote::ToTokens`, so can be directly used within the
`quote!` macro. It expands to a reference to the matched field.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.binding)

`binding: `[Ident](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.106/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Ident.html)The name which this `BindingInfo` will bind to.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.style)

`style: `[BindStyle](https://docs.rs/enum.BindStyle.html)The type of binding which this `BindingInfo` will create.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/synstructure/lib.rs.html#350-410)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-BindingInfo%3C'a%3E)### impl<'a> [BindingInfo](https://docs.rs/struct.BindingInfo.html)<'a>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/synstructure/lib.rs.html#350-410)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-BindingInfo%3C'a%3E)

### impl<'a> [BindingInfo](https://docs.rs/struct.BindingInfo.html)<'a>

`BindingInfo` references

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/synstructure/lib.rs.html#407-409)#### pub fn [referenced_ty_params](https://docs.rs#method.referenced_ty_params)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&'a [Ident](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.106/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Ident.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/synstructure/lib.rs.html#407-409)

#### pub fn [referenced_ty_params](https://docs.rs#method.referenced_ty_params)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&'a [Ident](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.106/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Ident.html)>

Returns a list of the type parameters which are referenced in this field’s type.

[§](https://docs.rs#caveat)Caveat

If the field contains any macros in type position, all parameters will be considered bound. This is because we cannot determine which type parameters are bound by type macros.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
let di: syn::DeriveInput = syn::parse_quote! {
    struct A<T, U> {
        a: Option<T>,
        b: U,
    }
};
let mut s = Structure::new(&di);
assert_eq!(
    s.variants()[0].bindings()[0].referenced_ty_params(),
    &["e::format_ident!("T")]
);
```

# Structure in synstructure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/synstructure/0.13.2/synstructure/struct.Structure.html

`pub struct Structure<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A wrapper around a `syn::DeriveInput` which provides utilities for creating
custom derive trait implementations.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Unlike `Structure::new`, this method does not panic if the provided AST
